(Photo by Soobum Im/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a series of injuries depleted the Oklahoma City Thunder depth, the preseason favorite signed wing Dalen Terry to a two-year deal, per ESPN’s Shams Charania . While further financial details were not disclosed, it seems most likely that Terry’s deal pays him the veteran’s minimum and is fully non-guaranteed. With the Thunder missing Jaylin Williams, Cason Wallace, and Chet Holmgren for months, Terry will get a chance to audition for a bigger role. If he struggles to find his footing, he will likely be waived for another addition. Terry spent the summer and preseason competing for a spot on the Golden State Warriors roster. While Terry fell short of a full NBA deal, he was slated to be a centerpiece for the Santa Cruz Warriors, Golden State’s G-League affiliate this season. However, the Thunder have changed those plans. The Chicago Bulls drafted Terry with the 18th overall pick back in the 2022 NBA Draft out of Arizona. He appeared in 218 games over his first four seasons, but was unable to show enough potential to convince a team to dedicate a rotation spot for him heading into this season. The Bulls had declined Terry’s fifth-year option, and dealt him to the 76ers at last year’s deadline. After failing to get an NBA deal in free agency, he joined the Warriors a series of deals over the summer. A 6’6 wing who just turned 24, Terry remains an intriguing 3-and-D prospect. The fact that an organization as renowned for scouting and development as the Thunder is willing to give him a trial window further endorses that side of things. Nevertheless, he has averaged just 3.5 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.2 assists on 44.3%/31.4%/63.8% shooting in 11.2 minutes per game over his career.

stories.title: It’s fun to be a Sixer right now
stories.summary: Wine and dancing don’t normally mix with basketball, but don’t tell these Sixers.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 02: LeBron James #23 of the Philadelphia 76ers celebrates with Tyrese Maxey #0 during the second half of a game against the Chicago Bulls at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 02, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images LeBron James famously loves wine. Typically, he enjoys drinking it when he’s not playing, but apparently exceptions can be made. On Monday night, James went into the crowd going after a loose ball in the third quarter of the Sixers’ 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls. There was a brief stir from the fans. We later found out it was because James had taken a sip from a spectator’s cup. “I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine,” James said. “So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm, man. How good it was.” So, how good was it? “It was alright,” he said. Spoiled by California wines, no doubt, but James is profiling well with his new team. When James’ agent Rich Paul did his media blitz during his client’s free agency, he mentioned happiness as the biggest factor for the King’s decision. In the fourth quarter, as the Sixers began to pull away, James found himself guarded by the 6-foot-1, 190-pound Tre Jones. LeBron easily bullied Jones into the post. Jones bit on a fake and Leonard Miller came over to help. James pump-faked again, this time getting Miller in the air, absorbing the contact and burying a short fadeaway. All of which led to a fun celebration. And on the next offensive possession, it was Tyrese Maxey’s turn to get into the lane and convert a crazy finish while getting fouled. And another celebration ensued. THESE TWO >>> 😎 pic.twitter.com/KvkQjMVhQd — NBC Sports Philadelphia (@NBCSPhilly) November 3, 2026 Safe to say, this group is having a good time. “Listen, it’s a long marathon,” James said, “and if you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it — even though you’re working, even though you’re locked in — it could wear on you. So for me, especially at this point in my career, too, being able to just appreciate the moments, the small moments. These fans are great to us. We try to be great to them as well by playing the game the right way, playing the game hard, and then also just being showmen as well.” James finished the night with 15 points, nine assists and seven rebounds. Maxey with 26 points and 11 assists. Jaylen Brown had 25 points, 11 rebounds and five assists. Joel Embiid, who was on a minutes restriction while managing plantar fasciitis, recorded 15 points, eight rebounds and three assists. The Sixers as a team had 36 assists on 48 makes. Tough night for the “there’s only one ball!” crowd. And let’s not forget about VJ Edgecombe — you know, the guy whose growth was going to be stunted because the Sixers have too many good players. The second-year guard scored a season-high 21 points, his first 20-plus point game on the young season, and dished out five assists. It was a rewarding scoring night for a guy who’s done all the dirty work for the Sixers’ starting group. Edgecombe said his lower usage rate isn’t his concern, though. “I don’t get antsy or impatient or anything,” he said. “We’re 7-1 and that’s the most important thing. … And like tonight, I was able to get going a little bit, but once you just find that joy out there, just playing basketball … I was just kind of hard on myself early [this season] because I was missing shots I [usually] make and that’s not on nobody else but me. And like I say, it’s fun when you’re winning. I don’t want to be a cancer because I ain’t getting the shots that I want to get. I’m still learning. I’m in year two.” The chemistry between the starting group is growing. A 7-1 start is a big help, but there seems to be an eagerness for all of them to learn each other. It’s something that’s been going on since training camp. In fact, a lesson from camp made its way onto the game floor. James hit Edgecombe with not one but two absurdly accurate bounce passes in transition, but the pair needed to build trust to execute them when it counted. “There’s a couple times in training camp that he kind of slowed up and didn’t think I’d get the pass there to him,” James said. “And I told him all he has to do is just run, and I’ll try to put it on time, on target as much as I can.” After the game, Edgecombe described it as a teaching moment. He was rewarded for that diligence. Against the Bulls, Edgecombe was ready, flushing down multiple transition opportunities. “If you’re open, he’s going to pass it to you,” Edgecombe said. “The main thing is just being ready. Tonight, I had to run to go get them.” It’s a fun time to be a Sixer. And this team is still in the fermentation process. “It’s a lot of talent, man,” Brown said. “And we like each other and we’re just kind of like building that chemistry of how we can get this thing to a well-oiled machine. So I think we’re taking steps forward every single day. I think we still got a long way to go to be a really, really solid, great team. But we’ve been able to win some games. We started out the season 7-1 and you haven’t seen our best version yet. So that’s a good sign.”

stories.title: Draymond Green tackles opponent, brawls with another for 26th career ejection
stories.summary: Another day, another incident for Draymond.
stories.detailText: Draymond Green’s reputation precedes him, and it was on full display Monday night against the Suns. Green was tossed for a double technical after he tackled Khaman Maluach, then got physical with Dillon Brooks after the play — seemingly trying to choke him. Draymond Green was assessed a double technical on this play and was ejected. pic.twitter.com/uCmsTQxmcX — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 3, 2026 Not sure we can really call this a “choke,” it was more like he grabbed Brooks’ jersey and twisted it around him, but either way, it was completely out of line. This all kicked off because Maluach ran into Draymond, but it wasn’t exactly the hardest hit we’ve ever seen. Definitely didn’t warrant Green channeling his inner linebacker to tackle Maluach on the play. We’re now on record watch with Draymond when it comes to career ejections. This incident led to number 26 on his career, needing only three more to tie Rasheed Wallace, who had 29 over the course of his career. It took Wallace 16 years to hit that mark, and this is the 15th year of Draymond’s career — so never say never. Maybe that’s the point of all this? Nail a few more ejections and ensure his place in history. The NBA has not commented on the incident yet, though it’s possible Green will face a suspension.

stories.summary: The biggest mistake in Wolves history is finally fixed
stories.detailText: NEW YORK - JUNE 25: (L-R) Jordan Hill, Stephen Curry, Hasheem Thabeet, NBA Commissioner David Stern, Ricky Rubio, Blake Griffin and James Harden pose for a portrait during the 2009 NBA Draft on June 25, 2009 at the WaMu Theatre in New York, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2009 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images CONTINUATION OF THE “WHAT IF” WOLVES SERIES . IN THIS SERIES, I PLAY THE ROLE OF TIMBERWOLVES OVERLORD AND GO BACK IN TIME AND RIGHT SOME OF THE WRONGS OF OUR FAVORITE FRANCHISE. SINCE THIS IS THE TIMBERWOLVES, THERE ARE A LOT OF WRONGS. THIS SERIES MAY GO ON FOREVER. “ What If” Wolves Volume 6: “Khan, you bloodsucker!” – Captain James T. Kirk or JetAllen When the Minnesota Timberwolves acquired LaMelo Ball this offseason, I found myself asking a simple question: did the Wolves finally solve their point guard problem? Early returns are optimistic at this point. Some good games, some not so. But based on history, what else should we expect from this franchise? The Timberwolves have been through point guard after point guard. None of them seem to last long, if at all. This team has been going through PGs like Spinal Tap goes through drummers. RIP Peter James Bond. The Timberwolves started off by taking what they thought was a franchise cornerstone in Pooh Richardson, their first-ever draft pick. We have previously discussed why that didn’t work out in the first “What If” Wolves article . Since picking Pooh, the Wolves have struggled to find a franchise player at the one. There have been some solid players, even All-Stars, but they were always short stints. The point guard problem should have been solved by now, and hopefully it finally is with Ball, but repeated mistakes have left this position in a constant state of flux. I had originally planned to write an article focusing only on the reign of terror brought to this franchise by former General Manager David Kahn. But my liquor cabinet was only half-stocked at the time, and I would need copious amounts of booze to relive that whole ordeal. Instead, we will focus on one issue. One teeny, tiny issue that I consider the biggest mistake in franchise history. David Kahn was on the job for exactly 33 days (trust me, I counted) when he made quite possibly the greatest trade in Timberwolves history. Kahn traded former Rookie of the Year Mike Miller and guard Randy Foye to the Washington Wizards for Etan Thomas, Darius Songaila, Oleksiy Pecherov, and the fifth pick in the upcoming 2009 NBA Draft. Only Pecherov would ever play for the Wolves (44 games), but the prize of the trade was the pick. With the addition of the fifth overall pick, MN would now draft back-to-back with the fifth and sixth picks. With the fifth overall pick in the 2009 NBA Draft, the Timberwolves selected my (and Leo’s) favorite player of all time, Ricky Rubio. NEW YORK – JUNE 25: Ricky Rubio, selected number five overall by the Minnesota Timberwolves poses for a portrait during the 2009 NBA Draft on June 25, 2009 at the WaMu Theatre in New York, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2009 NBAE (Photo by Jennifer Pottheiser/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Rubio was a dynamic PG from Spain. His list of accomplishments overseas was incredible: he turned pro at 14 years old, won the Rising Star Award, FIBA Young Player of the Year Award, was named Spanish ACB League’s best point guard, Defensive Player of the Year, and won a EuroLeague Championship. Quite the trophy room. But I believe what put Ricky at the top of the draft class was his final performance of the 2006 Europe Under-16 Championship, where he scored 51 points, grabbed 24 rebounds, had 12 assists, and stole the ball 7 times. One of the greatest games ever played. Rubio also held his own in the 2008 Olympic Finals against the USA, where Ricky went up against the likes of Jason Kidd, Dwyane Wade, Chris Paul, and Kobe Bryant. To me, Rubio was a lock with the 5th pick in the draft. But man, did Kahn ever mess up the next pick. This is where the “What If” Wolves will take over, fire Kahn immediately, and take the player that I was begging the Timberwolves to take. I remember the draft like it was yesterday. I was sitting on the couch at my in-laws’ house. My son was born a few months prior, so we were at the grandparents’ house to get some baby relief. And I was yelling at the television. David Kahn was on the job for exactly 34 days (trust me, I counted again) when he made the biggest mistake in Timberwolves history. Kahn had drafted Jonny Flynn. With Ricky Rubio in the fold, my thoughts were to get him a lights out shooter that can pair with him in the backcourt. Rubio had already proven that he could lock down defensively (yes, bigger guards would have been a problem, but only a few teams had elite big guards that operated out of the post), so the other guard could take on the smaller matchup. So who was the best shooter in the draft? Not Jonny Flynn, I can tell you that. With the 6th overall pick in the 2009 NBA Draft, the “What If” Wolves selected Wardell Stephen Curry II from Davidson College. NEW YORK – JUNE 25: Stephen Curry, selected seventh overall by the Golden State Warriors speaks to Mark Jones of ESPN during the 2009 NBA Draft on June 25, 2009 at The WaMu Theatre at Madison Square Garden in New York City, New York. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2009 NBAE (Photo by David Dow/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Steph Curry was the best story coming out of the 2008 NCAA Tournament. Curry owned March Madness that year by beating larger schools Gonzaga (40 points), Georgetown (30 points), and Wisconsin (32 points) before eventually losing in the Elite Eight to Kansas (25 points). Curry would leave tiny Davidson College the following year after being named to the All-American First Team, leading the nation in scoring (28.6 ppg), and shooting 41% on three-pointers for his college career. In my eyes, Curry was the perfect complement to Ricky Rubio (Watch how effortless Curry’s game is in the video below). So why did Kahn select Flynn over Curry? David Kahn compared Flynn and Rubio to Hall of Famers Earl Monroe and Walt Frazier of the New York Knicks . I can sort of see the familiarities with the flash of Rubio and Monroe along with the defense of Flynn and Frazier. But both Pearl and Clyde could score. Flynn couldn’t shoot a lick, finishing his career shooting 33% from three and 40% overall from the field. Don’t get me wrong, Rubio shot just as bad for his career, but he found a way to average double digits in scoring for his career, plus he was an elite set-up man. According to NBC Sports’ Kurt Helin, even the Wolves players and coaches were baffled by the draft . This is why Curry was the right pick from the get-go. There were also some issues with good ol’ dad when it came to drafting Steph Curry. Dell Curry was a great shooter with the Charlotte Hornets in the 90s (40% career three-point shooter) and taught his boys how to let it fly. He also was trying to force his eldest son to get drafted by the Knicks, who owned the 8th overall pick. That’s right. Dell didn’t want his kid to go to the Golden State Warriors either. So why did they not listen to the father’s threats? Well, they didn’t have David Kahn as a GM, and since the “What If” Wolves fired Kahn, neither do we. We ignore Dell’s wishes and take Curry right after Rubio. David Kahn looking over his shoulder as he is about to be fired. | NBAE via Getty Images Now, if this fantasy scenario plays out according to my plan, the Timberwolves don’t have to wait two years for Rubio’s arrival like in reality. Ricky comes over as an 18-year-old PG prodigy with impervious knees. Steph plays at the shooting guard position offensively. Being off-ball saves his ankles a bit, and his career trajectory starts on a more positive note. Rubio and Curry switch defensively, and both play the passing lanes for easy steals. Rubio now has a more open lane to finish at the rim due to the actual threat of a Curry three-pointer (Wolves shot 34% as a team in 2009-10). The pace of play is quickened after great outlet passes from Kevin Love. And the “What If” Wolves become a playoff contender for the first time since Kevin Garnett was traded to Boston. Hell, KG might even come back earlier if he gets to play with Rubio and Curry. Rubio may still eventually be traded, or he retires to go back home to Spain, but Curry would then slide over to the point, and all would be right in the world. Curry would go on to possibly beat out KG as the best Timberwolf of all time. As a consolation, he would at least go down as the best point guard. Unless Melo gets us a chip. Just for fun, here is a top ten list of the most games started at the point guard position for the Timberwolves. Ricky Rubio – 384 games started (two separate stints) Pooh Richardson – 212 Luke Ridnour – 201 Terrell Brandon – 197 Mike Conley – 179 Stephon Marbury – 163 D’Angelo Russell – 157 Michael Williams – 150 Jeff Teague – 124 Sam Cassell – 119 Bonus: Jonny Flynn – 89 games started for the Timberwolves (only a three year NBA career) Bonus Bonus: Stephen Curry – 1065 regular season games started for the Golden State Warriors, 149 playoff games started. Bonus Bonus Bonus: Steph would’ve been too miserable to start any games with his prized golf courses covered in snow.

stories.detailText: Giannis Antetokounmpo had very high praise for Luka Doncic following the Lakers’ 138-117 win over the Heat on Monday. Doncic finished with 42 points (14-for-24 from the field, 6-for-15 from 3), seven rebounds, 13 assists and two steals, notching his fourth 40-plus point performance in the last five games as the Lakers improved to 6-2. “Obviously he’s one of the best scorers to ever play this game, if not the best,” said Antetokounmpo, who had 30 points, 12 rebounds, seven assists, one steal and two blocked shots. Luka Doncic (77) of the Los Angeles Lakers plays defense on Giannis Antetokounmpo (7) of the Miami Heat on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026, at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. NBAE via Getty Images “Right now?” asked a reporter. “Not right now,” Antetokounmpo said. “Of all-time. I feel like some people are scared to say that. But it’s got to be out there. He’s also an elite passer.” Doncic is averaging a league-leading 38.3 points on 50% shooting from the field (43% from beyond the arc), eight rebounds and 8.1 assists this season. His 13 assists were a season high. In Monday’s win, Dončić became the first Laker player to score at least 20 points in the first half in five straight games since Kobe Bryant in 2007. Doncic is earning a lot of early MVP chatter . He has never finished in the top-two for the award despite leading the league in scoring twice (2023-24 and 2025-26) and carrying the Mavericks to the 2024 NBA Finals. AP Photo/Jayne Kamin-Oncea When Antetokounmpo, a two-time MVP and one-time champion in 2021, was asked if Doncic should get more consideration for the award, he didn’t hesitate. “Is he an MVP-caliber player?” Antetokounmpo asked. “I think, no doubt. He’s been up there. He’s definitely up there this year. Like, what he’s doing is incredible. And not only that, but his team is winning, and their offense is good, everybody is being involved, they’re in a good place right now. So, yeah, a guy who’s averaging 38 and his team is winning, he’s definitely got to be in the MVP discussion.”

stories.title: Warriors ‘loved’ Draymond Green’s ejection: ‘Lit a fire in all of us’
stories.summary: Green’s ejection 2 minutes into the second half Monday night awakened the sleep-walking Warriors.
stories.detailText: SAN FRANCISCO — The first time Draymond Green and longtime nemesis Dillon Brooks shared the floor this season, only one of them was still left by the end. In that battle, consider Brooks the winner. In the one that actually matters in terms of wins and losses, point to Green and the Warriors. Green’s ejection 2 minutes into the second half Monday night awakened the sleep-walking Warriors, who erased a 17-point deficit in his absence to pull out a 116-113 win . “He lit a fire in all of us,” said Stephen Curry, “and we had to respond. So I’m glad we did.” Golden State Warriors’ Draymond Green (23) and Phoenix Suns’ Jalen Bridges (15) are separated by security in San Francisco on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. JOSE CARLOS FAJARDO/Bay Area News Group via AP While the double technical ended Green’s night and put him two closer to the 16-tech threshold that automatically merits a one-game suspension, the Warriors had no problem with it. In fact, just the opposite. “I loved it,” said fourth-year guard Brandin Podziemski, who had six points in the first half but finished with 20. “It fueled our team. We didn’t have that edge to start the game. … “Maybe he sensed it. Maybe he didn’t. But it helped.” Green wrapped both arms around Khaman Maluach as Phoenix’s 7-foot center tried to finish at the rim shortly into the third quarter and threw him to the ground. Almost as soon as Maluach hit the floor, Brooks was in Green’s face, a familiar juxtaposition for two of the NBA’s most fiery players. Green responded by grabbing Brooks’ jersey with both hands, close to his neck. Golden State Warriors’ Draymond Green throws down Phoenix Suns’ Khaman Maluach during an NBA game at Chase Center in San Francisco, Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. JOSE CARLOS FAJARDO/Bay Area News Group via AP Upon review, the incident resulted in technical fouls for Green and Brooks, and a second on Green for his “throwdown” of Maluach. That earned Green an early trip to the showers. And almost instantaneously, the game flipped in the Warriors’ favor. They were trailing 68-57 when Green was tossed at the 10-minute mark. Not even four minutes later, the Warriors had rallied to tie the score at 73 and never trailed by more than six again. The Suns responded to Green’s absence by going small, subbing out Oso Ighodaro with 6-foot-7 forward Ryan Dunn at center. Coach Steve Kerr didn’t care to weigh in on Green’s testy back-and-forth with Brooks but said the Suns’ adjustment “opened up the game.” “I think they played maybe 12 minutes of super small with [6-foot-7 forward Ryan] Dunn at the five,” Kerr said. “It kind of opened up the game a little bit. Our crowd got into it and our guys just did a great job of finding energy on a back-to-back.” Stephen Curry (30) and Draymond Green (23) of the Golden State Warriors smile on the bench against the Denver Nuggets on Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Denver. NBAE via Getty Images While the Warriors were on the back end of their second back-to-back of the season, the Suns were well-rested having played Friday. When they squared off Monday night, it was the Warriors’ eighth game of the season to only the Suns’ fifth. So even though Green and Curry sat out against the Clippers the night before, it was understandable for the Warriors to come out sluggish. The fact that they were able to rally and finish stronger, well, maybe some credit belongs to the guy who spent most of the second half in the locker room. “We’ve got to have our brother’s back when he defends us,” Curry said. “But it’s also one of those games, most of the guys on the back to back, Phoenix had been off for a couple days, they started 1-3 and [we] knew they were gonna come out playing desperate. … “We just tried to weather the storm, execute, give ourselves a chance, and that third quarter was the run that we needed to get back into it.”

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - NOVEMBER 2: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs smiles during the game against the Utah Jazz on November 2, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images It’s giving midseason. Somewhere in the second quarter, with the Spurs up one and about to be up more, I realized I wasn’t watching the game. I was, instead, watching myself not watch the game, which is a worse hobby and the one I’m apparently best at. The game was fine. The game was exactly what it said on the label: a nondescript tilt between two teams already headed down different tracks. The shine of October basketball had worn off completely and, like summer turning to fall, the Grind had arrived. Shocking how quickly that happens. As a first quarter blowout turned into a 2nd quarter snoozer, my brain began to wander a bit. I could be anywhere in the world right now. A plastic stool in Hanoi, a bowl of pho, a little light rain. A mountain pass in the Andes, thin air, nobody asking me for a take. Man, I should be reading books. Seeing films. I should be the kind of person whose passport has all those cool stamps in it. This one precious life the universe handed me was unraveling in real time as Ace Bailey stepped into a 25-foot pull-up three to cut the Jazz’s deficit to one. Then Stephon Castle missed a layup and I almost decided to call it a night. It was as annoying as it was unremarkable and I just didn’t need it anymore. I reached for the remote and, as I did, Victor Wembanyama, who a minute earlier had similarly flubbed an alley-oop, grabbed the rebound and tipped it back in. Twenty seconds after Bailey’s three. No celebration. Barely a facial expression. I’d love to tell you that’s the moment I’d been looking for, but that would be too tidy. What I’d been searching for was a hook. A story, a cause, a catalyst. Anything to hold off the particular ennui of being a fan of a good team. And Wemby wasn’t even good last night, not by any stretch. Five of fifteen. Zero for five from three. Five turnovers. He was in that mode he gets in from time to time where he decides the Key to Victory is to simply chuck it. The Spurs won by 22 anyway, not because of a miracle but because this roster has more than one way to be competent. The Spurs are, mercifully, more than the sum of their parts. Not that the parts are bad. Quite the contrary. Dylan Harper scored all 17 of his points before the third quarter was half over. Stephon Castle is an animal. De’Aaron Fox looks like the guy we paid for. Tarris Reed continues to grab rebounds in a way that feels like it’s going to be important (seven in about seven minutes last night). Every wing combination we’ve thrown on the court is its own kind of fun. I mean, look at Harrison Barnes. A man as old as time itself (he’s four years younger than me) had an insanely active night. He knocked down threes from 29, 25 and 24 feet, he ran around, he caused trouble. Early in the fourth he got tangled up with Brice Sensabaugh, slid across the floor, got back up, and just stared at him while the refs reviewed it in slow motion. I’m told that clip racked up 140,000 views on the world wide web within about an hour. The thing about the Grind is that it doesn’t have to mean anything, which means that everything within the Grind gets to be exactly what it is. A tip dunk. A well executed outlet pass. An old man staring down Brice Sensabaugh. Like, I didn’t come out of the womb craving the Larry O’Brien trophy. I just was at my breakfast table in 1996 watching Michael Jordan dunk on Rik Smits during a SportsCenter rerun, and some part of me said, with zero strategic vision, “Yes. More of that.” More of that was the entire ask and, frankly, it still is. Look at us. You and me. Like I said, we could be anywhere in the world right now, but we’re right here with the Spurs and the Jazz on a Monday night in November. The stools in Hanoi will still be there someday, but a precocious superstar, having the worst night of his season, is putting a ball back through the hoop like a child tucking in his stuffed animals for the night. You don’t have to impress some greater importance on a moment like that to make it mean something. You were there. It’s a part of you now and you got to live it. If that isn’t special, I don’t know what is. The beautiful game. pic.twitter.com/bX57x1dKoA — J.E. Skeets (@jeskeets) November 3, 2026 Takeaways Dylan Harper seems almost casually good at basketball. It’s remarkable and breathtaking, these things he’s doing, but it also has that effect of seeming effortless when he’s casually dismantling another team. In the second quarter he stole the ball and in a blink Vassell was dunking off his pass. In the third, he stole it again and Stephon was finishing an alley-oop before I’d even registered it. He added 8 assists and 7 rebounds on top of all his scoring. I find myself almost taking it for granted at this point, and we’ve really only started to scratch the surface of what he’s capable of. Scary to think about! (For our opponents. For us it’s just exceedingly cool and fun.) I know it’s just the Jazz, grain of salt and all that, but I never get tired of seeing the Spurs get out on the break and run. They won fast-break points 26-9, against a Jazz team that turned it over just 11 times, a season low for Utah, so a lot of that was pure rebound-and-go. They also won the paint 52-36 and opened the game on an 18-2 run. Run for days my boys. Grab the ball and never stop running. Only good can come from this. Open looks from three, easy paths to the rim, potential foul trouble for the opponents. Push that pace. Push that pace. PUSH THAT PACE. This is not how development works and, to be clear, I don’t know what I’m talking about, but I absolutely crave Tarris Reed minutes. I want him to become a Sasquatch, Godzilla, King Kong, Loch Ness, Goblin, ghoul and a zombie with no conscience. I want basketballs to fear him checking into the game because they’re about to get rebounded to within an inch of their lives. I love a wire-to-wire win. Next time you hear me complaing about a wire to wire win feel free to come to my house and take an ice cold waterloo out of my fridge as payment for my sins. WWL Post Game Press Conference So, you’re a Waterloo Man, eh? I’m a man of all seasons, to be clear, but right now, yes, I am currently in a Waterloo phase of my Sparkling Water career. Any particular reason? There is a particular Black Cherry flavor I’ve grown fond of and I just can’t stay away at this point. It scratches this weird nostalgic part of my brain that yearns for a Blue Sky soda I had in my youth. Do you remember Blue Sky soda? Vaguely. That had kind of cool cans? Yeah, the cans were cool. I don’t know. I think I had just never experienced the concept of a soda that existed outside the mainstream world of the Coca-Cola and Pepsi family trees, so when I went on vacation and saw this crazy looking can with a cherry sitting on a cloud it just… broke my brain a little bit and I had to have it. Did it taste good? Who could say? I was six years old. I’d left the summer heat in Texas and woken up the next day in a Colorado mountain town sipping an alien soda from heaven. Maybe it was good, maybe it wasn’t, but it stirred something deep in my soul that I think I’ve been searching for ever since. And Black Cherry Waterloos scratch that itch for you? They do. Publix also pretty regularly throws them in Buy One Get Ones for me and who am I to turn down a deal like that.

teamStories.detailText: Things you might not know about Memphis Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome , the 29-year-old journeyman averaging 28 points per game for one of the NBA's most surprising teams : Jerome played in the first 16-1 upset in NCAA tournament history, when he and Virginia were stunned by UMBC in 2018. (Jerome and the Cavaliers would win the title the next season.) He played two seasons with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander in Oklahoma City . He played one season with Stephen Curry in Golden State . Something front offices around the league are surely aware of by now: Jerome can become an unrestricted free agent next summer. Jerome, a starting guard for ESPN's Contract Year All-Stars, headlines a 12-player roster full of potential impact free agents, many of whom are searching for massive paydays in the 2027 offseason. We're also providing early predictions on each player's next contract and the likelihood of getting moved by the February trade deadline. Let's run down the roster. Jump to: Starters | Reserves How we selected the roster We disqualified players who have previously made an All-NBA or All-Star team. That means you won't see potential summer free agents such as the Washington Wizards ' Anthony Davis , New York Knicks ' Karl-Anthony Towns , Miami Heat 's Giannis Antetokounmpo , Milwaukee Bucks ' Tyler Herro -- or even Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James , who holds a player option for 2027-28 -- on this list. Players with team options in their current contracts, such as the Knicks' Josh Hart and LA Clippers ' Rui Hachimura , also were not considered. After all, if a player is outplaying his deal enough to be considered a Contract Year All-Star, it is highly unlikely his team will decline the option. Finally, we have kept off potential 2027 restricted free agents, such as the Detroit Pistons ' Daniss Jenkins . STARTERS Fred VanVleet , Rockets 2026-27 stats: 12.2 PTS | 6.8 AST | 1.7 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: VanVleet is averaging his fewest points per game since 2018-19 but has steadied the Rockets' offense. After missing all of last season with a torn ACL in his right knee, the 32-year-old guard is averaging 6.8 assists with only 1.0 turnovers per game. As a result, Houston's assist rate has improved from 27th in 2025-26 to 13th in the early going this season. Prediction: The Rockets will advance deep into the playoffs and re-sign VanVleet in unrestricted free agency. Despite being in the final year of his contract, VanVleet is not extension-eligible because he signed a two-year deal in 2025. How VanVleet factors into Houston's future could be determined by the franchise's finances. With Year 1 of Amen Thompson and Tari Eason 's extensions beginning in 2027-28, Houston is projected to be $10 million below the luxury tax and $19 million below the first apron. Ty Jerome , Grizzlies 2026-27 stats: 28.2 PTS | 5.7 AST | 42.1 3P% Contract status: 2027 player option ($9.7 million) Impact this season: Jerome was not a candidate last season because he played just 15 games, but the first two weeks of 2026-27 has made the 29-year-old an obvious choice for the starting 2-guard role. Jerome is shattering previous career highs, and Memphis is plus-18.2 points per 100 possessions with him on the court, per Cleaning the Glass. Prediction: If he continues to play at a high level, Jerome will decline his $9.7 million player option and become an unrestricted free agent. Because early Bird rights have been accrued, the maximum Jerome could sign with Memphis (or with another team if he is traded) is four years and $72.3 million. With eight teams projected to have cap space and another 12 with the $16 million non-tax mid-level exception, Jerome should have suitors outside of Memphis. If Jerome chooses to opt-in for next season, he becomes eligible to sign a four-year, $99.9 million extension. Ryan Rollins , Bucks 2026-27 stats: 11.0 PTS | 4.4 AST | 4.1 REB Contract status: 2027 player option ($4 million) Impact this season: Rollins is averaging seven fewer points per game than last year and is shooting 34.5% from the field and 26.3% on 3-pointers. Those down numbers, plus the fact that the retooling Bucks are 1-6, would normally preclude a player from this list. But the Contract Year All-Star selection process factors in much more than the first two weeks of the season. With Rollins averaging career highs in points (17.6 per game), assists (5.6) and rebounds (4.6), Milwaukee was nearly six points better when he was on the court in 2025-26. Prediction: Rollins declines the option and becomes an unrestricted free agent. Rollins signed a three-year contract with the Bucks in 2025 but is not extension-eligible until summer 2027; to sign a long-term pact, Rollins would need to decline his player option and re-sign with Milwaukee as a free agent. He could opt-in to his $4 million contract for 2027-28 and sign up to a four-year, $100 million extension. Michael Porter Jr ., Nets 2026-27 stats: 20.7 PTS | 7.0 REB | 1.6 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Porter is averaging at least 20 points per game for the second consecutive season, but the 28-year-old forward is doing more than just scoring: His 1.6 steals per game (with 2.5 deflections) is a career high, and Brooklyn's defense is eight points per 100 possessions better with Porter on the court. Prediction: Porter gets traded to a contender before the Feb. 11 deadline. Since July, Porter has been eligible to sign a four-year, $236.5 million extension with Brooklyn. If the Nets move him, Porter would become eligible to sign for three years and $154 million with his new team. He can also elect to become an unrestricted free agent in the summer of 2027, regardless of his post-deadline future. Paul Reed , Pistons 2026-27 stats: 13.4 PTS | 6.7 REB | 65.0 FG% Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Reed has taken advantage of a surge in minutes (13.9 per game last season to 26.9 in 2026-27) following starting center Jalen Duren 's hamstring strain. Reed has nearly doubled his points per game and is shooting a career-high 65% from the field. The Pistons are plus-12.9 points per 100 possessions with Reed on the court. Prediction: Reed, not extension-eligible because he signed a two-year contract with Detroit, will hit unrestricted free agency. Reed's increased role should only boost his free agent stock as one of the top frontcourt options next summer. Nearly two-thirds of teams have at least $16 million to spend in free agency. The Pistons, meanwhile, are $24.5 million below the luxury tax but do have flexibility with the non-guaranteed contracts of Duncan Robinson , John Collins and Isaiah Joe . RESERVES Kris Dunn , Clippers 2026-27 stats: 9.0 PTS | 4.7 AST | 2.9 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Dunn ranked fourth in steals last season (trailing only Cason Wallace , Dyson Daniels and Ausar Thompson ) and fifth in deflections. This season, his third with the Clippers, Dunn is averaging the second-most minutes in his career (29.7 per game) with a career-high 2.9 steals per game. The 32-year-old trails only Daniels for the most deflections this season. Prediction: The Clippers trade Dunn at the deadline and recoup one of the five future first-round picks docked after the NBA's salary cap circumvention investigation. Dunn then signs a two-year, $37 million extension with his new team to bypass free agency. Davion Mitchell , Heat 2026-27 stats: 16.0 PTS | 8.0 AST | 45.7 3P% Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Despite the Heat's 2-5 record, Mitchell is having a career year in minutes (33.5 per game), points (16.0), assists (8.0, third in the league) and field goal percentage (51.8%). And after recording double-digit assists in nine games last season, Mitchell is already up to four. Prediction: This truly could be too early. After three seasons with the Sacramento Kings and half a season with the Toronto Raptors , Mitchell seems to have found a permanent home in Miami. His next contract, however, will depend on Miami's cap flexibility. With Year 1 of Pelle Larsson 's extension beginning in 2027-28, Miami is projected to be $23 million below the tax and $32 million below the first apron. If Mitchell signs in the $15-16 million range per season, it is unlikely Miami has the full $16 million non-tax mid-level exception available to use next summer. (Because Mitchell signed a two-year contract with Miami, he is not extension-eligible during this season.) RJ Barrett , Raptors 2026-27 stats: 20.7 PTS | 6.1 REB | 4.0 AST Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: We were hesitant including Barrett, considering he is in the final year of a $107 million rookie extension signed in 2022 with the Knicks. Finances aside, Barrett has had three and a half impactful seasons since Toronto traded for him in December 2023. Barrett has averaged at least 19.2 points per game in the seasons since. Just as he did when Brandon Ingram was injured during the Raptors' first-round series this past postseason, expect Barrett to pick up most of the scoring load with Kawhi Leonard out indefinitely. Prediction: Despite being eligible to sign an extension since July, Barrett will become an unrestricted free agent. The Raptors are allowed to exceed the salary cap because of Barrett's Bird rights but face a financial crunch next season. With the first year of Leonard's and Jakob Poeltl 's extensions beginning, Toronto is projected to be $23 million below the luxury tax and $29 million below the first apron. Jonathan Kuminga , Timberwolves 2026-27 stats: 12.3 PTS | 5.4 REB | 44.1 3P% Contract status: 2027 player option ($6.4 million) Impact this season: Expect Kuminga to play a significant role with Anthony Edwards out for an extended period. The 24-year-old forward has started all eight games this season, averaging career highs in minutes (30.8 per game) and 3-point percentage. Defensively, Kuminga is averaging 1.3 steals and 2.8 deflections, and Minnesota boasts a defensive rating of 99.5 when the forward is on the floor. Two stats to monitor all season: Kuminga's 3-pointers (1.4 more attempts per game than last season) and free throw percentage (a career-low 55% this season). Prediction: Kuminga declines his player option to become a free agent for the third straight offseason. Because Kuminga has non-Bird rights and Minnesota is close to the first apron, the maximum first-year salary it can offer is just $7.2 million. That will be a non-starter in contract negotiations, with Kuminga signing elsewhere. Kenrich Williams , Thunder 2026-27 stats: 6.0 PTS | 3.4 REB | 47.4 3P% Contract status: 2027 Unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Williams likely does not make the list if Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace were healthy. But because the two starters will miss most (if not all) of the season, expect Williams' minutes to soar. In the 37 games as part of the rotation last season, he averaged 8.2 points and shot 36.3% from the floor. Prediction: With another financial crunch looming in Oklahoma City, Williams becomes an unrestricted free agent and signs elsewhere in the offseason. His salary next season starts at $6 million, comparable to the tax midlevel exception. Keldon Johnson , Spurs 2026-27 stats: 9.3 PTS | 5.6 REB | 1.1 AST Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: The reigning Sixth Man of the Year appeared in every game last season, breaking the record for points by a reserve. But in the playoffs, Johnson scored double-digits in just five of the Spurs' 16 games. This season, Johnson's touches are down nearly 20% and he is shooting 2.5 fewer 3-pointers per game, but he is making a more concerted effort to attack the basket. Through six games, Johnson had scored 79% of his points in the paint. Prediction: Until there is more clarity on the financial situation next season, San Antonio will table extension talks with Johnson. With Year 1 of Victor Wembanyama 's extension beginning in 2027-28, San Antonio is projected to be $11 million below the luxury tax and $18 million below the first apron. Even without Johnson re-signing, the Spurs are likely a luxury tax team when factoring in the 2027 first-round pick from Atlanta and a filled-out roster. Moussa Diabate , Hornets 2026-27 stats: 9.1 PTS | 9.5 REB | 1.8 STL Contract status: 2027 unrestricted free agent Impact this season: Diabate has transformed from two-way player to perhaps the best offensive rebounder in the NBA. Thanks to Diabate's league-best 5.4 offensive boards per game, Charlotte ranks sixth in that category and 11th in second-chance points. Across the past two seasons, the Hornets are 37-16 when Diabate starts. Prediction: Diabate signs a four-year, $64 million extension on Feb. 8, his first day eligible. (The $16 million first-year salary is comparable to the non-tax mid-level exception next season.) Even with extensions for Brandon Miller and Diabate kicking in for 2027-28, Charlotte would still have flexibility below the luxury tax and apron.

NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The San Antonio Spurs continued their three-game homestand on Monday night and used two strong quarters to put away the Utah Jazz, earning the 119-97 win at the Frost Bank Center. The win is the fifth straight for San Antonio, who defeated the Jazz for the second time in nearly a week. San Antonio set the tone from the opening tip, being aggressive by slicing into the paint at every chance and using their signature ball movement to find the open man for a shot. Defensively, the Spurs put together their best quarter of the season so far, holding Utah to 16 points, the lowest they’ve allowed in the first quarter this season, and 27 percent shooting. The second quarter saw Utah make a run, cutting the Spurs’ lead to 36-35. Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson was furious and called a timeout, pounding his fist into his hands in frustration as his team walked over to the bench. After that timeout, San Antonio responded with a 14-5 run to take a 50-40 lead and would eventually go into the locker room with some motivation to put the game away in the second half. San Antonio opened the second half by outscoring Utah 21-18, but another timeout from Coach Johnson saw him not happy with his team’s transition defense as Keyonte George hit a three in transition. The Spurs responded by closing the quarter on a 23-11 run to take full control going into the final 12 minutes. “Just not getting bored on what was working,” San Antonio guard Stephon Castle said after the game when asked about the second half surge. “I think we came back out in the 2nd half and brought that same kind of energy.” The Spurs were led by a balanced attack as seven players were in double figures by the final horn. Dylan Harper led San Antonio with 17 points, eight assists, and seven rebounds. Castle rebounded from his poor outing with a migraine on Saturday to score 16 points to along with five rebounds and four assists. Victor Wembanyama and De’Aaron Fox each chipped in 12, while Wemby pulled down 11 rebounds. Keldon Johnson led the Spurs’ second unit with 15 points and seven rebounds. “We have so many weapons,” Castle said of the Spurs’ balanced attack after the game. “We have so many guys who can make a play out of nothing, and we’ll be fine either way.” The injury-depleted Jazz were led by Lauri Markkanen’s 22 points as Utah lost its fifth straight. With the Spurs’ homestand closing on Wednesday night with a visit from Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks, Keldon Johnson said the team is not satisfied with a five-game winning streak after climbing out of the 0-2 hole to start the season. “We’ve yet to play our best brand of basketball,” he said after the game. “We’re getting better each and every game. If we felt like the best version of ourselves at this point of the season, we’d be in trouble. We’re improving and will continue to improve.” Game Notes Harrison Barnes came off the bench to score 10 points and left the internet with a pretty funny moment that will surely turn into a meme by the time this article goes live. Luke Kornet continued his strong play from Saturday night, scoring eight points and pulling down five rebounds in 16 minutes. If this is the version of the backup big the Spurs can consistently rely on, it will be huge for the non-Wemby minutes. On the other side, Carter Bryant continues to have growing pains as the enters his second season in the NBA. At one point in the game, Mitch Johnson subbed Bryant out for a quick conversation, sent him to the bench for a few moments and then put him back into the game. That was shades of Gregg Popovich from Coach Johnson, using these games as teaching moments that will benefit Bryant later in the season and in his career.

stories.summary: The Colts and defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore have agreed to terms on a two-year, $35 million extension, a source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.
stories.detailText: The Indianapolis Colts and defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore have agreed to terms on a two-year, $35 million extension, a source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo on Tuesday. The deal, negotiated by agent Kenny Zuckerman of Priority Sports, includes a $13 million signing bonus and $22.5 million in new money through 2027. The Colts rebuffed trade interest in Adebawore and instead finalized the extension with the defensive tackle, who has already matched his career high with four sacks in just eight games this season. The Colts, who fired general manager Chris Ballard earlier this month, have already traded guard Quenton Nelson (to the Seattle Seahawks ) and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner (to the San Francisco 49ers ) as they begin a rebuild amid a 2-6 start. The Colts are engaged in trade talks with multiple teams regarding star running back Jonathan Taylor , sources have told ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Josh Downs , the team's top wide receiver with Alec Pierce currently on injured reserve, has also requested a trade. Adebawore, 25, has 10.5 sacks, 13 tackles for loss and 20 quarterback hits since being selected in the fourth round by the Colts in 2023.

stories.detailText: {"unknownError":"There has been an error","expiredError":"This video has been expired due to copyright restrictions.","unavailableError":"This content is not yet available.","georestrictedError":"This content is not available in your location.","networkId":"169843","adManagerUrl":"https://mssl.fwmrm.net/libs/adm/6.51.0/AdManager.js","serverId":"https://29773.v.fwmrm.net/ad/g/1","profileId":"169843:nbcu_web_jwp_cs_moat_https","afid":"140315314","caid":"nbcs_nbc_pft_vikingsqbs_261103","csid":"nbcsports_embed_on_domain","sfid":"","adHocGroup":"","athlete":"","businessUnit":"NBC Sports","category":"","duration":"181048","event":"","externalAdvertiserId":"nbcs_nbc_pft_vikingsqbs_261103","genre":"News, Trending","guid":"nbc_pft_vikingsqbs_261103","league":"NFL","network":"","platform":"PC","playlist":"","show":"ProFootballTalk","sport":"Football","subtype":"","team":"Minnesota Vikings","title": "Could O’Connell move off Murray as Vikings QB?","datePublished":"","videoPageUrl": "https://www.nbcsports.com/watch/nfl/profootballtalk/could-kevin-oconnell-move-off-kyler-murray-as-minnesota-vikings-starter","availableDate":"2026-11-03T13:50:35Z","expirationDate":"","countries":""} How can the Vikings bench Kyler Murray without benching Kyler Murray? They can rely on an injury through which he otherwise would be able to play. It's hard not to look at the current status of Murray's hamstring "tightness" as cover for a soft benching of Murray. That gives the Vikings a chance to let Carson Wentz, who played well enough in most of the Week 1 win over the Packers and all of the Week 2 win over the Bears. While the Vikings will never admit to that strategy, consider this undeniable fact: On Tuesday, offensive coordinator Wes Phillips was asked for an assessment of Murray's play "in the past couple weeks." "I don't really want to get into, like, overarching, 'Hey, this is this is the . . .," Phillips said. "You know, the fact of the matter is, you know, we lost the game against a tough [Lions] football team on the road. It's a division game. It stings, but we've got to get better moving forward. And, you know, we'll see as the week goes on, where we're at in that spot . . . but, yeah, we've got to get better. We're going to actively pursue every avenue we can to make that happen." This implies, if taken literally, pursuing every avenue toward acquiring an upgrade via a trade — whether that's Jacoby Brissett, Daniel Jones, Kirk Cousins, or even Justin Herbert. It all comes down to whether the Vikings are content to keep doing what they've been doing, or whether they'll make a move aimed at significantly upgrading a position that, in recent weeks, has not been good enough. Yes, they're 6-1. That's better than anyone could have expected them to be. But it's not because Murray has turned the clock back to the early years of his career. His passer rating (86.6) is toward the bottom of all qualifying quarterbacks (and, in fairness, that's higher than the numbers generated by Brissett, Jones, and Herbert). It's the lowest number for any season of Murray's career, and the overall performance is less than what the Vikings need to maximize their current formula. Especially since he's not getting the ball to receiver Justin Jefferson. That's something Wentz did consistently in 2025, making Wentz the preferred option to J.J. McCarthy — who returned to the lineup following a Week 2 ankle injury only after Wentz suffered a season-ending shoulder injury in Week 8. If McCarthy was still in Minnesota, there would be an unavoidable groundswell to give him a shot. But he lost the No. 2 job to Wentz. Which means Wentz won it. Which means that the Vikings could be thinking about giving Wentz a Monday night audition against the Bills, with a plan to make a possible trade the next day if things don't go well. For now, the rest of the week will reveal whether and to what extent Murray or Wentz will take the first-team reps at practice. And whether Murray or Wentz will play on Monday night. It won't be a surprise if it's Wentz against the Bills. Even if Murray is technically healthy enough to play.

stories.detailText: The New Orleans Saints are on the kicker market. The Saints announced on Tuesday that they have released veteran kicker Daniel Carlson after Carlson missed another field goal in Sunday’s 16-10 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Carlson missed a 52-yard attempt with 9:42 remaining that would have cut Pittsburgh’s lead to 16-13. He finished the game hitting 1 of 2 field-goal attempts, dropping his season success rate on field goals to a career-low 66.7% (8 of 12). Carlson hit all of this field goals up to 49 yards with the Saints, but was 3 of 7 on attempts from 50-plus yards. His release ends his tenure with the Saints after seven games. stories.detailText: TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love was placed on injured reserve because of a high ankle sprain that will sideline the rookie for four to five weeks. Love, the third overall pick in this year's NFL draft, previously had been dealing with a different ankle sprain this season. The former Notre Dame star will miss a minimum of four weeks while on IR. Love walked off the field in the first half Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys and slammed his helmet to ground on the sideline. After being looked at by trainers, he went into the blue injury tent and later walked to the locker room. Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Love's most recent ankle issue isn't related to his preseason or early-season ankle injuries, one of which happened to each ankle. The first injury occurred against the Raiders in Arizona's second preseason game, and the second came early in the season. "It's a new portion of the ankle," LaFleur said Monday. "So, I'll keep it at that." Love has rushed for 268 yards and one touchdown over six games during his injury-plagued rookie campaign. Veteran Tyler Allgeier replaced Love as Arizona's primary running back Sunday, gaining 191 yards from scrimmage and scoring two touchdowns in Arizona's overtime victory in Dallas.

stories.title: If Rams don’t trade for a WR, more work CJ Daniels?
stories.summary: Sean McVay says the Los Angeles Rams don’t need to trade for a wide receiver, they have CJ Daniels
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: CJ Daniels #6 of the Los Angeles Rams gets set during the second quarter of a preseason NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sean McVay had heavy praise for rookie receiver CJ Daniels as McVay presented Daniels as a potential solution for the team, and any perceived lack of receiver depth. McVay has been asked as the trade deadline approaches if the Rams are looking to add to their wide receiver room, and so far, the head coach publicly has leaned more towards a “No” than a “Yes” . Instead, verbally opting to see other players return from injury, and step up on the depth chart. Enter Daniels, a Day Three pick in the 2026 NFL Draft who the Rams traded up to acquire . Daniels hasn’t accumulated any stats at the NFL level, yet, but McVay hints that Daniels, rather than a trade , could be an answer for the Rams at their receiver position as they move forward. The Rams have Puka Nacua, Davante Adams is on IR, and after them there is second-year veteran Konta Mumpfield and veteran Ram Tutu Atwell, but no one has been able to fill the void left behind by Adams, and if Nacua goes down, who can Matthew Stafford reliably throw to? Said McVay on how the Rams can bolster their wide receiver room for the last half of the season, “I do think there’s some guys on the roster that are capable of being able to step-up if their number’s called. Whether you’re talking about Tutu, I think Mumpfield’s done a nice job with his opportunties. There’s a guy in CJ Daniels that’s really done a hell of a job that you’re gonna see get more opportunities.” What does more playing time for Daniels look like? Will he be featured in the offense in a meaningful way? McVay keeps his answer vague, which is fair as he doesn’t want to tell other teams what his plans are, but one telling aspect is that McVay does say that he’s not going to hand out chances that could hurt the team. So, it begs the question, is Daniels ready to help the Rams now, or does he need more time to develop? “I would never rule out opportunities to get better, but at what opportunity cost? And you gotta be able to figure out for what does that look like for the long and the short.” If Daniels is ready, and if he performs well-enough to prove McVay right, then the Rams were correct in standing pat at the trade deadline. If Daniels isn’t ready, and if Nacua misses time, then McVay may regret the decision not to trade for a wide receiver before the deadline, and or not adding more help through the draft . The Rams are taking a gamble if they don’t add more depth, and according to McVay, not adding more depth could mean they are betting on Daniels.

stories.detailText: (Photo by Evan Bernstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have been connected to several wide receiver possibilities as the NFL trade deadline approaches, but one prominent name appears to be off the table. ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter poured cold water on speculation surrounding a potential trade for New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson, making it clear that he does not expect the former first-round pick to land in Pittsburgh. The speculation gained traction after NFL insider Jason La Canfora suggested Pittsburgh could be ambitious ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline and potentially pursue another playmaker. Wilson was among the names mentioned as a possible fit alongside DK Metcalf, giving the Steelers another weapon in their passing game. However, Schefter made it clear that the connection between Wilson and Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers should not be viewed as a reason to expect a reunion. “I was told last week; no way they trade him.” Schefter said on his podcast Tuesday. Wilson and Rodgers spent two seasons together with the Jets in 2023 and 2024, but reports have indicated that their relationship was not particularly strong toward the end of their time together. Schefter suggested that people speculating about the reunion might not understand the full dynamic between the two. “I don’t think people know that full relationship there. I don’t know that that would work. That’s not happening. Garrett Wilson’s not being traded to Pittsburgh.” There are also significant reasons New York would be reluctant to move on from Wilson. The 26-year-old signed a four-year, $130 million contract extension in 2025 and remains a central piece of the Jets’ long-term plans. He also has not requested a trade, despite the team’s struggles this season. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, enters its bye week with a 6-2 record and sits in a strong position in the AFC North. With the trade deadline approaching, the Steelers could still explore ways to strengthen their receiving corps as they look to make a legitimate postseason run. They were 0-5 when they traded Walker, ending the 1989 season at 1-15. It wasn’t the five players the Cowboys received from Minnesota that were important, but rather the conditional draft choices that would come if players Dallas acquired were cut the next offseason. Ultimately, the trade landed them Emmitt Smith, Kevin Smith and Darren Woodson, and gave them flexibility to make other moves. stories.title: With Lamar Jackson on IR, Ravens name undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano starting QB vs. Jaguars
stories.summary: This will be Joe Fagnano's first career start.
stories.detailText: Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told the media Tuesday the team will start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano on Thursday against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The announcement comes as starting quarterback Lamar Jackson was added to injured reserve with a thumb injury , and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley was diagnosed with turf toe. Minter added that Huntley could also be going on IR. Fagnano will be the second undrafted rookie to start under center for Baltimore in the Ravens' 32-year history, per ESPN's Jamison Hensley . In Baltimore's loss to the Buffalo Bills last week, Jackson lasted just one snap before he hit a defender on a pass attempt. He immediately came off the field holding his throwing hand and did not return. Huntley took over, but then suffered a lower-body injury (later deemed turf toe) that forced Baltimore to use Fagnano, the team's emergency quarterback. In relief, the rookie completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Fagnano also ran the ball three times for 3 yards. The rookie ended his collegiate career at UConn after starting it at Maine in 2019. He played 24 career games for the Huskies, totaling 5,252 passing yards and 48 touchdowns. Fagnano is less mobile than Jackson or Huntley and rushed for just 223 yards and 4 touchdowns on 93 carries in college. The injuries in the quarterback room aren't limited to Jackson and Huntley; Fagnano was also spotted at Tuesday's practice wearing a guard/brace on his right ankle. The injury must be minor enough that Minter felt confident naming the rookie starter for Thursday. With the quarterback room depleted, Baltimore signed two quarterbacks to back up Fagnano. The Ravens signed Austin Reed to the practice squad on Monday and Kedon Slovis on Tuesday. CBS Sports researcher Doug Clawson noted that Baltimore's current backup quarterback room — Fagnano, Reed and Slovis — has fewer career passing touchdowns (0) than starting running back Derrick Henry (4). Fagnano is looking to become the first UConn quarterback since Dan Orlovsky in 2011 to win an NFL start, per Hensley . Baltimore is 4-4 and has lost three consecutive games. The loss to Buffalo was Jackson's first game since Week 4. Now, with Fagnano under center, the Ravens face the 5-2 Jaguars, who are currently first in the AFC South.

stories.title: Steelers Week 8 grades in win over Browns
stories.summary: Steelers grades in win over Browns.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off their most dominant performance of the season in a 27-6 clobbering of the Cleveland Browns. The win puts Pittsburgh at 6-2 going into the bye and just a half game back of the top seed in the AFC. As we do every week, Joey Bray and I are here to give you our grades from the Steelers’ biggest win of the year. QB Aaron Rodgers Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers didn’t light up the stat sheet, but he didn’t have to when the Steelers ran for 200 yards. He did, however, lead a 44 second touchdown drive at the end of the first half that served as the dagger into the Browns’ chances of winning, and he hit Darnell Washington on multiple chunk passes downfield. If DK Metcalf holds onto a ball that hits him in the chest, Rodgers’ stat line looks better and doesn’t have an interception. Grade: B- Joey Bray: Aaron Rodgers was just along for the ride in this one, and that’s not a bad thing at all. His 13-25, 172 yards, and an interception stat line is easily one of the worst we will see this season from Rodgers. However, you never watched this game and thought Rodgers was playing poorly. With the Steelers up multiple possessions for most of the game, and running the ball as well as they were, it was a low stress game for the veteran quarterback. He stayed clean and moved well, taking only one sack, which matters as the Steelers will undoubtedly have to rely on Rodgers more and more down the stretch. Grade: C RBs Jaylen Warren & Rico Dowdle Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers’ running back duo had their best game as a tandem, racking up a combined 199 yards and two touchdowns. Jaylen Warren tied his career high of 143 rushing yards, while Rico Dowdle had his best game as a Steeler with 56 yards and the game’s first score. This is the Steelers’ offensive identity – pound the rock with these two backs and dare you to stop them. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: The Steelers have an identity offensively, and it’s running the damn football. Jaylen Warren has the second most scrimmage yards in the NFL through eight weeks, and is the most efficient running back in the NFL on a per-touch basis. Warren’s breakout season coupled with Rico Dowdle’s emergence over the last few weeks has given the Steelers a true two-headed monster in their backfield. Both backs got in the end zone and controlled the pace of the game as the Steelers cruised to an easy victory. Grade: A+ WR DK Metcalf Jarrett Bailey: This is just unfortunately who Metcalf is. He isn’t a No. 1 receiver. One catch for four yards is beyond unacceptable for the money he is making. Grade: F Joey Bray: It’s simply impossible for anyone to defend Metcalf anymore. It’s not just that the receiver isn’t making an impact, but he’s actively costing the team. Rodgers hit Metcalf right in the chest as the receiver bobbled the ball, which eventually led to an interception. With the Steelers up multiple possessions, it didn’t end up mattering much in terms of the outcome of the game. However, drops and frustrating plays have been the theme of the Steelers’ most expensive offensive player. The team almost certainly needs to add a weapon at the deadline so they don’t have to rely on Metcalf down the stretch. Grade: F Offensive line Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers led the NFL in EPA per rush in Week 8. They’ve led the NFL in that stat since Week 3. Aaron Rodgers also faced the third-lowest pressure percentage in Week 8. The offensive line has become one of the game’s best. Can’t say enough about how tremendous this group is. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: Tell a friend to tell a friend the Steelers have an elite offensive line. It is something to behold seeing just how far this offensive line has come along since they slid rookie Max Iheanachor and veteran Brock Hoffman into starting spots. Pittsburgh ran for 200 yards and only allowed one sack. The offensive line has suddenly become one of the strongest units on the Steelers roster. Grade: A Red zone offense Jarrett Bailey: If I see another fade to DK Metcalf after Aaron Rodgers clearly checked out of a called run, I’m going to launch a brick through my TV. Run. The. Ball. Pittsburgh still scored three red zone touchdowns, but this should have been a 38-6 win. Grade: C- Joey Bray: Stop throwing the goal line fades to Metcalf. It was especially curious to me that for as well as the Steelers were running the ball, they refused to run in goal to go situations. Whether it’s McCarthys playcalling, or Rodgers choice to throw the fades, they need to have a better collective plan moving forward. It’s hard to complain about much considering they won by multiple scores. But they will have to turn those field goals into touchdowns if they want to establish themselves as a serious contender in the AFC. Grade: D EDGE T.J. Watt Jarrett Bailey: Watt has officially returned to elite form. He had two sacks against the Browns, giving him 7.5 on the season – he had seven all of last season. He leads the NFL in sacks, and his pressure to sack percentage is fourth in the league (min. 100 pass rush snaps). Grade: A+ Joey Bray: At the midway point of the Steelers season, TJ Watt is on pace for 15 sacks. Watt added two to his total on Sunday as the Pittsburgh pass rush feasted on the Browns’ offensive line. The veteran edge rusher is defying all odds by having a career rejuvenation in 2026. Watt has once again become a player who can change the game in an instant. Grade: A+ Pass rush Jarrett Bailey: Eight sacks is an absurd number. It was great to see Alex Highsmith register five pressures. Highsmith, T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward, Patrick Queen, Kevin Jobity, and Keeanu Benton all registered at least half a sack, and the Steelers had a combined 31 pressures. Just tremendous work. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: Whenever you can sack the opposing quarterback eight times, you have a good chance of winning the game. The Browns were not able to handle the Steelers’ pass rush whatsoever on Sunday. The blitzing even got creative, as linebacker Patrick Queen recorded a sack and a half in the contest. This was a display of just how lethal the Steelers’ pass rush can be down the stretch for Pittsburgh. Grade: A+ Defense Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers were fifth in the NFL in EPA per play in Week 8, and they didn’t allow the Browns to reach the end zone. Overall, they’ve allowed just one second half touchdown this season, which is an insane stat. This unit has turned into one of the NFL’s best. Grade: A+ Joey Bray: You cannot ask for much more than holding your opponent to season lows in points and rushing yards, and that is exactly what the Steelers did on Sunday to Cleveland. The pass rush and linebacker play were immaculate and a large part of why the Steelers dominated this game from start to finish. Patrick Graham deserves all of the credit for the way he has this defensive playing with a secondary that still has some question marks. Grade: A+ Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!
