stories.title: The Best Team in the NFL is the Chicago Bears
stories.summary: The Chicago Bears beat the Seattle Seahawks and made a statement to the rest of the NFL: the best team in the league resides in Chicago.
stories.detailText: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates a win against the Seattle Seahawks after the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears are dominating the NFL, and the rest of the league is finally starting to notice. Maybe it’s because so many people hate Caleb Williams and they won’t believe it. Maybe it’s because the Bears have been so bad for so long, it’s hard to believe this is actually them. Or maybe it’s that Caleb Williams was hurt and the Bears went 2-2 in the 4 games he missed all or part of the game. Whatever the reason, the way the Bears have played the last three games leaves you with only one logical conclusion: The Chicago Bears are the best team in the NFL. These stats speak for themselves: Since Caleb Williams has returned from injury, the Chicago Bears have led for 158:33 of 180 minutes. They have only been tied at 0-0. They have never trailed. — Bill Zimmerman (@BillTZimmerman) November 3, 2026 The Bears are dominating right now. And they aren’t dominating the Tennessee Titans and the Arizona Cardinals. In the last two weeks, the Bears did this against the two teams that met in the Super Bowl just nine months ago. The way this team is playing, and with the addition of Jeffery Simmons, something has happened with my expectations that I haven’t had since I was a child. Never in my adult life have I truly believed the Bears can win the Super Bowl. Maybe that makes me overly critical. Maybe that just makes me a realist, but let me try to explain. To me, there are two types of good teams: playoff contenders and Super Bowl contenders. The Bears have been playoff contenders on more than one occasion. In 2018, you knew they were headed for the playoffs. During the Lovie years, you knew the Bears were good enough to play additional football in January. But did you ever truly believe they were going to win a Super Bowl? Did you truly believe it? Or did you just hope they could? In 2006, I never truly believed they could beat the Colts. How was Rex Grossman going to beat Peyton Manning? In 2018, if the Bears did, in fact, take down Sean McVay again and reach the Super Bowl? Did we really think Matt Nagy and Mitch Trubisky could outduel Bill Belichick and Tom Brady? You could hope that things would align just perfectly and somehow, someway, the Bears could pull out a miracle win and bring home a title, but did you truly believe they were a Super Bowl contender? The last time I felt this way was in 1987. The Bears still had Jim McMahon. Walter Payton was still on the roster. The ‘85 defense was still largely intact. This was the last time I felt this way. I was 10. Did I actually know what I was watching? No, of course not. I was a hopeful child who believed my team could win. Why not? They won just two years before; why couldn’t they do it again? I didn’t understand that Payton was on his last legs. I didn’t understand that McMahon had no chance of staying healthy. I didn’t understand how much Wilber Marshall would be missed and that other key pieces on the defense were aging. I didn’t understand the context. Now I do. I’ve never had this belief and this level of confidence in this team in my adult life. The Bears have the coach. They have the quarterback. They have the offensive line. They have the weapons. They have the defense. The Bears have everything they need to win it all. The team isn’t perfect. If they can land Khalil Mack and make this defensive line even stronger, they should. If they can land a CB and beef up their secondary, it’s a must. Spend what you have to do to make this happen. Draft picks are for teams that aren’t drafting with the last spot in each round, and that’s where the Bears are headed if they keep this up. This Chicago Bears team can win the Super Bowl. That should be the expectation. If the Bears aren’t playing a game in Los Angeles on February 14th, I’m going to be disappointed. That’s an awesome feeling to have on November 3rd. Is there a team you are afraid of in the NFL? The only team that should give you any concern in the NFC is the SF 49ers. In the AFC, it’s the Buffalo Bills. Are you afraid of the Kansas City Chiefs? I’m not. Right now, the Bears have a more talented roster. They have the better coach. They have the better quarterback (Yes, I know what I said). This offense is the best in the NFL. When it’s rolling, no defense in the league can stop it. Ask the Seahawks; they stop everyone and still gave up 34 points. This defense, with Jeffery Simmons, is a whole new ballgame. As we talked about last week, Simmons is so good, he makes everyone around him better. We saw that already in his first game. Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Devin Bush- they all looked fantastic. The Chicago Bears have arrived. There’s no team in the league better than this one. You can have concerns about the secondary; you can have concerns about their depth; you can have concerns. You should have concerns. No team in the league is perfect. But despite any of those concerns, one thing is clear: The best team in the NFL resides in Chicago.

stories.title: Sione Vaki emerges as Lions' change-of-pace back to pair with Jahmyr Gibbs
stories.summary: Even though the Lions have only played seven games and most teams have played eight, Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is leading the NFL with 191 touches — a huge workload that raises questions about whether Detroit needs a player to share carries with Gibbs, the way David Montgomery had done before he was traded to Ho…
stories.detailText: Even though the Lions have only played seven games and most teams have played eight, Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs is leading the NFL with 191 touches — a huge workload that raises questions about whether Detroit needs a player to share carries with Gibbs, the way David Montgomery had done before he was traded to Houston. Enter Sione Vaki. Vaki had a career-high 11 carries and a career-high 65 yards in Sunday's win over the Vikings, and his direct running style was a valuable change of pace for the Lions to have while Gibbs got some breathers between his own 23 carries for 153 yards. Lions coach Dan Campbell emphasized after the game that the Lions told Vaki they needed him to step up against the Vikings, and Vaki answered the bell. "Vaki was one of the guys we challenged this week going into this game," Campbell said. "We were going to need him. He needed to show up. He was going to need to get some carries for us, some significant carries. They needed to be real yards, and he was going to need to be able to pass protect for us. And I thought he took a big step today. That's a huge step. He gained a lot of trust today, a ton." Lions quarterback Jared Goff said the entire offense is excited about what Vaki can bring. "Vaki ran his tail off," Goff said. "And when he's able to do that, it just gives Gibbs that much more of a breath on the sideline to come back and do his thing at his full capacity. And the O-line loved it. They loved the challenge of, like, we're going to keep leaning on you guys. And I thought they played great." The Lions think they have the best running back in the league in Gibbs. If Vaki can prove to be one of the better backup running backs in the league, the Lions' running game will be in very good shape.

stories.title: Sam Darnold’s cratering play is a big picture problem for the Seahawks
stories.summary: The Seahawks have won a Super Bowl with Sam Darnold, but this version of Darnold may slam Seattle’s window to contend shut.
stories.detailText: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold is a Super Bowl champion who played an important part in bringing another Lombardi Trophy to Seattle, and that can never be taken away. Sam Darnold is also playing bad football. You can blame the offensive coordinator, you can blame the offensive line, you can blame the lack of a running game, but Sam Darnold is playing bottom-tier football. His worst throw from Monday night’s blowout loss against the Chicago Bears didn’t even count, but it’s emblematic of his incomprehensible decision-making. Sam's worst throw of the night was on a play that didn't count because of a defensive hold. This is not viable quarterback play. pic.twitter.com/ntueC8TChD — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 3, 2026 Incidentally, the play design is pretty much DOA but there is no need to turn 2nd and 1 into a double coverage gamble. Darnold’s touchdown-to-interception ratio is barely 1:1 over his last 16 regular season starts. His mostly great playoff run is the break-up in what is otherwise a prolonged stretch of play that is far removed from much of his 2024 Minnesota Vikings season and the first 10-ish games of his Seahawks career. Sam Darnold in the second half of last season with Klint Kubiak calling plays: 19th in air yards per attempt 19th in comp % over expected Dead last in EPA per play This is not new. He's been figured out. — Seahawk Nerd (@SeahawkNerd) November 3, 2026 Sam Darnold from last year's Rams loss until now: 334/551 for 3,936 yards, 23 TDs, 17 INTs, and a sub-6.0 ANY/A. His ANY/A plummeted toward the back-end of last season. Darnold's downturn didn't start with Fleury. There's a clear inflection point. No run game crutch this time. — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 3, 2026 (Editor’s note: It’s 344/551 and not 334) There are no advanced stats that can positively spin Darnold as an above-average starter at the moment. He really wasn’t playing particularly well for most of the back-end of 2025, but the running game finally sprung to life and Seattle’s defense and special teams repeatedly either scored or gave the Seahawks extremely short fields. The 2026 Seahawks are 4-4, which is not the end of the world, but how they’ve gotten to 4-4 is pretty much the worst case scenario in the short- and long-term. If Mike Macdonald’s defense hypothetically had curiously dropped off to be a middling group and the Seahawks were losing shootouts while Darnold was putting up impressive numbers, I think we could live with that and acknowledge that defenses can be more volatile year-to-year than offenses. Darnold is heavily culpable for at least three of the four defeats, and even his best game against the Washington Commanders is significantly impacted by what was effectively a game-losing pick-six. Darnold’s contract is a great mid-level contract for someone with his track record and roughly two seasons worth of good productivity. It’s also a contract that expires in 2027 , and the current version of Darnold does not look like someone who should be Seattle’s Week 1 starter, much less the starter in 2028. Barring substantial improvement over the second half of the season, John Schneider has a major decision to make on Darnold, regardless of whether or not Brian Fleury is still the offensive coordinator. We’ve seen Darnold be very good when paired with the right play-caller, and I am not going to put the failures of this offense exclusively at his feet. But Darnold is in that tier of quarterback who needs way more help to be functional than the likes of Josh Allen or Joe Burrow or Patrick Mahomes. Every quarterback needs at least some semblance of foundational support to succeed, but Sam needs way more stuff than, say, prime Russell Wilson. That includes, seemingly above all else, having an experienced and effective play-caller who can play to his strengths and minimize his worst habits. Brian Fleury does not seem to fit the bill. Darnold also needs play-action to work like we need air to breathe. When it’s not working, Darnold has consistently been anywhere from average to ruinous in pure dropback situations. He needs an offensive line to protect him so well that his pressure rate is low, otherwise this is what you get. Per ESPN Research, Sam Darnold was pressured on 14 of 39 dropbacks against Chicago. While pressured, he went just 1 of 11 for 13 yards and an interception. Here was Darnold postgame: pic.twitter.com/aeAYKUP4FP — Brady Henderson (@BradyHenderson) November 3, 2026 Darnold with a clean pocket and/or the ability to get the ball out of his hands quickly can sling it with the best of them. When he is dealing with pressure in his face, he is barely a starting caliber quarterback. We have two years of evidence in a Seahawks uniform. Sam Darnold was 30th out of 33 qualifying QBs in EPA/dropback when pressured, but he was also one of the least pressured QBs in the NFL last year. He's 31st out of 31 QBs in EPA/dropback when pressured in 2026, and he's top 12 in pressure rate. — Mookie Alexander (@mookiealexander) November 3, 2026 In effect, Sam Darnold needs: Play-action to be so insanely efficient that it overrides the lack of non-PA success. Favorable game scripts such that his team is almost never trailing . Related : A top-5 caliber defense such that his team is rarely trailing. An offensive coordinator/play-caller who can scheme up easy-button throws for fun. Related : A cheat code for a WR1. An offensive line that can pass protect competently. An explosive running game in case none of the above works out or is figured out by NFL defenses. To which I echo the thoughts of Carter: A good QB doesn’t need this much insulation. — Carter (@carso0onnn) November 3, 2026 There’s nothing wrong with building a great environment around a competent but limited quarterback, but that also means a crevice turns into the Grand Canyon when said environment is even marginally worse. You can live with Darnold’s turnovers if he’s as efficient as he was in 2024 and 2025. That is not even close to what we’re seeing in 2026. The possibility also cannot be discounted that two years of film effectively exhausted all of the routes that the likes of Kevin O’Connell and Klint Kubiak could make Darnold thrive. As I wrote not too long ago , “With non-elite quarterbacks there are only so many levers you can pull before competent defenses respond.” If Seattle sticks with Sam then it will likely need an(other) offensive coordinator to get him back on track, all while not being an immediate head coach candidate. This is the downside of having a defensive minded coach and your OC hires are either bad (see: Grubb, Ryan) or are so good that NFL teams take notice (see: Kubiak, Klint). The churn truly never stops unless you find that unicorn who can be a stable part of your organization while being no threat to hold a head coaching job. Seattle’s roster as a whole is a very good one; most of the players from last year’s Super Bowl squad are still here. Any premise of Seattle having a sustained window of playoff and Super Bowl contention was contingent upon Darnold sustaining his success and mercifully giving us all a break from debating Seattle’s next franchise quarterback. If Darnold cannot recapture even half of what made him go from draft bust to unlikely Super Bowl champion—this includes the rest of this year and (if applicable) his contract year in 2027—the Seahawks’ long-term vision is suddenly a lot more complicated. Drew Lock is a free agent and frankly I don’t want to bank on the QB revival thing yet again for a career backup entering Year 9. It’s not like Drew himself hasn’t had a history of being turnover prone with volatile week-to-week performances when he was a starter elsewhere. Jalen Milroe is a great unknown outside of preseason, and 2027 is a pivotal year for him to see if he’s even ready to be an NFL starter. Other than that? Seattle might find itself once again dealing with major uncertainty at the most important position in the sport. That’s what stings the most, even coming off an unforgettable Super Bowl season. The Seahawks have their head coach, have a lot of hyper-talented, young core pieces under contract either on rookie deals or massive extensions, but quarterback has become a giant question mark now and therefore makes for a much murkier future than hoped.

stories.detailText: Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in. Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. **UPDATED AS OF TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 3 AT 3:30 PM ET** AFC East ◆ Buffalo Bills The Bills emerged from their Week 8 win over the Ravens absent any fantasy-relevant injuries. ◆ Miami Dolphins De’Von Achane - RB (knee) Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season. Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright . The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season. ◆ New England Patriots Mack Hollins - WR (calf) Hollins departed the team's Week 4 win over the Bills with a calf injury and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve in Week 5. Impact: Veteran practice squad call-up Efton Chism saw the biggest increase in routes following Hollins' departure, which was particularly interesting considering the team's general lack of downfield abilities. Perhaps Kyle Williams could finally see additional time on the field. Romeo Doubs - WR (shoulder) Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum. Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined. A.J. Brown - WR (ankle) Brown was limited on Wednesday but downgraded to "DNP" Thursday and Friday, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins. Speaking to media Monday , head coach Mike Vrabel said, "We'll see," when asked if Brown would practice this week. Impact: Brown's absence leaves only DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism as healthy wide receivers currently on the roster. The most intriguing upside case to be made is with Williams in a potential full-time role on the perimeter, where his downfield acumen brings tantalizing ceiling. TreVeyon Henderson - RB (illness) Henderson was ruled out Saturday with an illness after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday. We'll get an update on his status Wednesday. Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson should operate as a clear workhorse for as long as Henderson remains sidelined, while Corey Kiner is in line to serve as the primary change of pace option. ◆ New York Jets Breece Hall - RB (quadriceps) Hall has missed the previous five games but is tentatively expected to return in Week 9 against the Chiefs. Impact: Hall would appear to be on track to resume lead-back duties for the Jets. Braelon Allen may have earned himself a weekly rushing role during Hall's absence, though we will not know for sure until this week's game transpires. Hall is a high-end RB2. Allen is flex-viable. AFC North ◆ Baltimore Ravens Lamar Jackson - QB (thumb) Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers , who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings. Tyler Huntley - QB (toe) Huntley suffered a turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills and is expected to miss "extended time." Impact: The Ravens suddenly find themselves in scramble mode to save a sinking season, with both Lamar Jackson and Huntley expected to miss significant time, the former of whom appears to be done for the season. Rookie Joe Fagnano came on in relief against the Bills and could not sustain drives, leaving the team in dire need of consistent quarterback play. They could address that need in the final week before the NFL trade deadline next Tuesday, but that is unlikely to take place before they face the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. Fagnano is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury and was seen wearing an ankle guard/brace in practice Tuesday. He is tentatively expected to start on Thursday. Joe Fagnano - QB (ankle) See above. Impact: See above. Adam Randall - RB (undisclosed) The Ravens activated Randall's 21-day practice window on Wednesday . Impact: Randall can be stashed in deep leagues. Durham Smythe - TE (Achilles) Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done. Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role. ◆ Cincinnati Bengals Andrei Iosivas - WR (thumb) The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3 Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable. Erick All - TE (knee) All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: All loses yet another season in devastating fashion after suffering his third torn ACL. His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki , although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy. ◆ Cleveland Browns Raheim Sanders - RB (hip) The Browns placed Sanders on injured reserve in Week 6 . Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed. ◆ Pittsburgh Steelers Michael Pittman - WR (foot) Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice . It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5 . The hope is that Pittman returns following the team's Week 9 bye. Impact: Pittman's absence opens the door for additional opportunities behind DK Metcalf , a role that now appears to be on rookie Germie Bernard 's shoulders following the multi-week injury suffered by Roman Wilson in Week 5. Ben Skowronek ( calf ) resumed practicing in Week 8. Roman Wilson - WR (finger) Wilson departed in the second half of Week 5 with a finger injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-game absence. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: See above. AFC South ◆ Houston Texans Jaylin Noel - WR (toe) Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats. David Montgomery - RB (groin) Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Montgomery is " week-to-week " with a groin injury. Head coach DeMeco Ryans failed to provide an update on the veteran back's status Monday after he missed the previous two games. Impact: The expected multi-game absence leaves Woody Marks atop the backfield depth chart. He is a viable FLEX starter, but the Texans showed in Week 6 that they will continue splitting backfield touches. Jawhar Jordan - RB (undisclosed) The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7 . Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined. Jayden Higgins - WR (knee) Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp. Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6. ◆ Indianapolis Colts Alec Pierce - WR (heel) Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3 . He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said Pierce won’t practice this week. Impact: Josh Downs should serve as the primary option through the air for as long as Pierce remains sidelined. The team signed veteran field-stretcher Darius Slayton in the wake of Pierce's injury, although he is unlikely to return weekly fantasy production. Slayton (knee) was ruled out for Week 5 on Friday. ◆ Jacksonville Jaguars Bayshul Tuten - RB (ankle/foot) Tuten was listed as a "DNP" on Monday's estimated practice report before failing to practice Tuesday , placing his status in doubt for Thursday's game against the Ravens. Impact: Tuten has emerged as a borderline workhorse for the Jaguars in recent weeks. An absence would boost the fantasy value of Chris Rodriguez, who would be a volume-based RB2 against the Ravens, should Tuten be unable to go. ◆ Tennessee Titans Tyjae Spears - RB (knee) Spears is listed as questionable in what seems like a weekly occurrence. He ultimately did not play in Week 7. Spears did not play in Week 8. Impact: Tony Pollard operated in a workhorse role in the absence of Spears in the team's Week 7 loss to the Browns, a setup that could persist should Spears miss additional time. Pollard is a middling RB2 without Spears in a difficult matchup. Carnell Tate - WR (shoulder) Tate did not practice throughout the week before being ruled out for Week 8 Friday. Impact: Wan'Dale Robinson is in line to serve as the top option through the air against the inside-funnel Cincinnati defense. He garners viable FLEX status. Fantasy managers will want to monitor the status of Tate through the team's Week 9 bye. AFC West ◆ Denver Broncos Pat Bryant - WR (ankle) Bryant suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 loss to the 49ers and is reportedly expected to miss "a few weeks." He was placed on injured reserve on Friday. Impact: Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims appear to be the next men up in Bryant's absence, although the team could use a "sum of all parts" mentality to bridge his absence, considering historical trends. Alpha wide receiver Jaylen Waddle would be the primary beneficiary. RJ Harvey - RB (knee) Harvey popped on the injury report Thursday with a knee injury and was ruled out for Week 8 Friday. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and will miss the next four weeks, at minimum. Impact: Harvey's absence returns the backfield to a two-way timeshare in the absence of Tyler Badie, with rookie Jonah Coleman the favorite for featured usage. Coleman can be started as a viable RB2 option in the coming weeks. ◆ Kansas City Chiefs Tyquan Thornton - WR (ankle) Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks. Impact: The return of Rashee Rice left little volume for the secondary options through the air in Week 8, a setup that appears likely to continue forward for the Chiefs. ◆ Las Vegas Raiders The Raiders emerged from their Week 8 win over the Jets absent any fantasy-relevant injuries. ◆ Los Angeles Chargers David Njoku - TE (fibula) Njoku is reportedly set to see his 21-day practice window opened in the coming days. Impact: Minimal. The Chargers have been the most disappointing offense in the league through the half way point of the season. NFC East ◆ Dallas Cowboys Jake Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson departed the team's Week 8 loss to the Cardinals with an ankle injury in the first quarter and did not return. Impact: Brevin Span-Ford is on hand to handle primary tight ends duties, should Ferguson miss time. He would not be a recommended streaming option outside of the deepest leagues. Malik Davis - RB (hip) Davis was placed on injured reserve and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Impact: The Cowboys released both Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah at roster cuts and now have only Emari Demercado on the active roster behind starter Javonte Williams . Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1. ◆ New York Giants Jaxson Dart - QB (knee) Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. He will undergo surgery to address the MCL and meniscus and miss the rest of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely. Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was benched in favor of recent acquisition J.J. McCarthy in the second half of their loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed McCarthy as the starter for Week 7. Cam Skattebo - RB (hamstring) Skattebo was seen working with trainers on Monday as he deals with a hamstring injury. Impact: Skattebo appears headed for change of pace duties in short order as the team continues to pursue Jonathan Taylor. More to come in the next few days as the trade deadline rapidly approaches. ◆ Philadelphia Eagles Saquon Barkley - RB (back/hamstring) Barkley returned from a two-game absence in Week 7, only to suffer an unrelated injury (back) in the second quarter. He played to little effect in Week 8 against the Comanders. Impact: Barkley is difficult to trust in a poor matchup considering his current ailments. Dameon Pierce and Tank Bigsby remain on injured reserve. Dameon Pierce - RB (undisclosed) Pierce was injured on a kick return in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 7 loss to the Cowboys. He was placed on injured reserve the following Wednesday . Impact: See above. DeVonta Smith - WR (hamstring) Smith was ruled out for Week 7 on Saturday. Smith has repeatedly aggravated the hamstring strain he initially injured in August. He remains sidelined to begin Week 8 and was ruled out Friday. Impact: Wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Britain Covey (knee) are also out for Week 8. Tight end Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon benefit. Tank Bigsby - RB (core) See above. Impact: See above. Jalen Hurts - QB (blood clots) Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. He was ruled out for Week 6 and could be looking at an extended absence. He was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after more clots were found in his lungs. Impact: Hurts is currently sidelined indefinitely. Tanner McKee enters the starting lineup under center following the release of Andy Dalton. The Philadelphia offense could be in trouble in the immediate future considering the sheer number of injuries. Will Shipley - RB (foot) Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot in Week 5. He is expected to miss multiple weeks. Impact: See above. ◆ Washington Commanders Terry McLaurin - WR (knee) McLaurin suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in Week 6. Impact: Treylon Burks should step into primary perimeter snaps, although he suffered an apparent injury late in the fourth quarter. No update has been passed on Burks as of Tuesday. Stefon Diggs will likely serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver moving forward. Jaylin Lane - WR (ankle) Lane suffered a dislocated ankle and fracture in Week 4 and is likely done for the season. Impact: Minimal. Lane was primarily a special teams contributor. Jacory Croskey-Merritt - RB (groin) Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice this week and ruled out for Week 6 against the 49ers. The team placed him on injured reserve on Saturday. Impact: Expect Rachaad White to fill in as the primary rusher, with Austin Ekeler on hand to soak up primary change of pace duties. White can be started as a viable FLEX option while Ekeler is likely best left on fantasy benches. Jeremy McNichols - RB (foot) McNichols suffered a foot injury in Week 8 that the team is currently testing to identify the severity of. Impact: Rachaad White and veteran Austin Ekeler are suddenly the only two healthy backs on the Washington roster, neither of whom is an overly exciting fantasy option on a struggling offense. White is the preferred option and could be started as a viable FLEX, should McNichols miss time. NFC North ◆ Chicago Bears Kyle Monangai - RB (thumb/toe) Head coach Ben Johnson labeled Monangai as " day-to-day " with a thumb injury suffered in Week 4, but he was later revealed to have suffered a turf toe injury as well. He remains sidelined for the Bears' Week 7 game against the Patriots on Thursday . He was ruled out for Week 8 Saturday. Impact: D'Andre Swift is an RB1. Roschon Johnson can be stashed. Cole Kmet - TE (knee) Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team's Thursday Night Football win over the Patriots. Impact: Expect Sam Roush to serve as the team's TE2 for the remainder of the season, while second-year tight end Colston Loveland should continue his recent ascension back into TE1 territory. ◆ Detroit Lions Isiah Pacheco - RB (back) Pacheco was placed on injured reserve to start the season. General Manager Brad Holmes said he "hopes Pacheco returns this season." Impact: Well, that doesn't sound great. There appears to be something more insidious going on with Pacheco's back than initially thought. Lions coach Dan Campbell said running backs Jacob Saylors and Sione Vaki could split touches behind Jahmyr Gibbs . Saylors appears to be the first player up. Gibbs handled an absurd 34 opportunities, of 37 total running back opportunities, in the team's Week 1, overtime win over the Saints ◆ Green Bay Packers Matthew Golden - WR (shoulder/foot) Golden gutted through multiple injuries on Thursday Night Football. Impact: None. Christian Watson - WR (chest) In one of the wilder stories of Week 8, Watson was knocked from Thursday Night Football with a chest injury , was taken by ambulance to the hospital, and returned in the second half to finish the game. Impact: Fantasy managers will want to monitor his situation in the coming week, although Watson appears to have avoided significant injury. Jayden Reed - WR (neck) Reed suffered a scary-looking neck injury that required stabilization in the team's Week 2 win over the Jets. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday that it is " way too early " to determine whether Reed will play again in 2026. That said, he was not placed on injured reserve ahead of their Week 3 contest. He will reportedly undergo surgery . Impact: Beyond the football implications, it is good to hear Reed avoided any life-altering injuries in Week 2. Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are likely to soak up additional snaps, although volume is most likely to concentrate on Christian Watson , Matthew Golden , and Tucker Kraft . Chris Brooks - RB (ankle) Brooks suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 4 win over the Buccaneers and is reportedly undergoing further testing. He did not play in Week 5 or Week 6. Impact: Brooks had been the most consistent rusher in a timeshare situation. Kaleb Johnson lost another fumble in Week 4, leaving MarShawn Lloyd as the likely beneficiary for as long as Brooks remains sidelined, although that role carries little value for the team with the fewest rush attempts in the league through the first month of the season. Skyy Moore - WR (ankle) Moore sported a walking boot instead of practicing on Wednesday . He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday . Impact: Should he miss time, the Packers' star players would further consolidate touches. ◆ Minnesota Vikings Kyler Murray - QB (hamstring) Murray was reportedly “slowed” by a hamstring injury in the team’s Week 8 loss to the Lions and is undergoing further tests to identify the severity. Impact: The injury appears to be of minor severity, meaning there likely isn't a change to his fantasy value moving forward. Don’t forget: Check out the Rotoworld player news feed for all the latest news, notes, and transactions around the league. NFC South ◆ Atlanta Falcons Brian Robinson - RB (hamstring) Robinson was limited on Wednesday before missing practice Thursday and Friday. He was ruled out for Week 7 on Friday. He remains sidelined to begin Week 8 before being ruled out Friday. Impact: This directly benefits lead back Bijan Robinson , who typically cedes meaningful touch counts to Robinson. ◆ Carolina Panthers Jonathan Brooks - RB (groin) Brooks aggravated the groin injury that forced him to miss the end of camp. The Panthers placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. He is expected to undergo core muscle surgery . Head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the team is "weighing" whether to open his practice window this week. Impact: Chuba Hubbard enters the volume-driven RB1 discussion in Brooks' absence. Trevor Etienne ( ankle ) is practicing in full and can be stashed in 14-team leagues, while AJ Dillon was ruled out. ◆ New Orleans Saints Travis Etienne - RB (hamstring) Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that the team is still deciding when to activate Etienne's 21-day practice window. Impact: Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller appear likely to split the load in Etienne's absence, neither of whom is overly enticing in fantasy circles in what is expected to be a shared workload. Jordyn Tyson - WR (hamstring) Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that the team is still deciding when to activate Tyson's 21-day practice window as the rookie looks to return from injured reserve. Impact: Fantasy managers waiting on Tyson's return could be forced to wait another week. ◆ Tampa Bay Buccaneers Jalen McMillan - WR (knee) McMillan suffered a sprained PCL in his first game action of the season in Week 3. The team placed him on injured reserve Monday, with an expected absence of 6-8 weeks. Impact: Not much change considering he made his season debut in Week 3, although rookie Ted Hurst should remain in the starting lineup. Emeka Egbuka - WR (foot/concussion) Egbuka was ruled out for Week 7 on Friday. He was limited to begin Week 8 but was ruled out due to his foot injury Friday. Impact: Wide receivers Chris Godwin (eight) and Ted Hurst (six) trailed Egbuka in targets (16) last week and are in line to benefit from Egbuka's absence. Tight end Cade Otton could also see additional volume over the middle of the field. NFC West ◆ Arizona Cardinals Jeremiyah Love - RB (ankle) The team placed Love on injured reserve after yet another ankle injury sustained in Week 8. Impact: Bam Knight suffered a concussion in Week 8 that could sideline him for Week 9 against the Seahawks. Tyler Allgeier suddenly finds himself atop the team's depth chart and can be started as a viable FLEX option in a difficult matchup. Jalen Brooks - WR (wrist) Brooks had emergency surgery on his wrist and will miss the remainder of the regular season. Impact: The team signed veteran Zay Jones Tuesday in an associated move. Expect volume to continue to remain heavily concentrated on Michael Wilson and Trey McBride . Elijah Higgins is notable for DFS purposes. Michael Wilson - WR (ribs) Wilson stated he is playing through two broken ribs following Sunday's comeback win over the Cowboys. Impact: Fantasy managers will want to track his status throughout the week closely, but it appears Wilson will play for as long as he can manage the pain. ◆ Los Angeles Rams Terrance Ferguson - TE (ankle) Ferguson aggravated an ankle injury in the team's Week 3 loss to the Broncos and was sent to injured reserve . As of Week 8, he needs more rehab time . Impact: Colby Parkinson (ribs) begins Week 8 sidelined. Tyler Higbee is a viable TE1/2 in fantasy if Parkinson sits out in Week 8. Davante Adams - WR (hamstring) The Rams placed Adams on i njured reserve with a ruptured hamstring tendon. He underwent surgery in Week 8, and head coach Sean McVay said his return timeline is “probably closer” to the shorter end of the expected 6-10 week timeline . Impact: Puka Nacua should see all the volume he can handle in the absence of Adams, while a shift to heavier rates of 12- and 13-personnel is likely in store for the Rams as they fight through another significant injury. Tyler Higbee suddenly finds himself a fantasy TE1, at least until Ferguson returns, while Nacua challenges for overall WR1. A recent ESPN report indicates the Rams will explore the trade market, though head coach Sean McVay denies it . Adams could be replaced as the team's No. 2 wide receiver while injured. Trading him away now could pay off. Colby Parkinson - TE (ribs) Parkinson did not play in Week 8. Impact: Davis Allen could warrant FLEX consideration in what is expected to be a 12-personnel-heavy offense. ◆ San Francisco 49ers Christian McCaffrey - RB (hamstring) McCaffrey was in and out of the lineup in Week 7 due to a hamstring injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan labeled as minor on Monday. He is expected to play in Week 9 following the team's bye. Impact: Fantasy managers will want to track McCaffrey's status closely considering his value to rosters, although the team's Week 8 bye should theoretically provide enough time to where he doesn't miss any games. Kaelon Black should be rostered everywhere. Mike Evans - WR (Achilles) Evans aggravated his Achilles injury in Week 6 and is expected to " miss some time ." He was ruled out for Week 7 on Friday but expected to return for Week 9 following the team's Week 8 bye. Impact: The hits to the San Francisco pass catchers continue as Evans now appears to be in line to miss at least Week 7. The team has its bye in Week 8, potentially setting up a situation where Evans misses only one contest. Expect volume to concentrate on Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle, with the team also expected to be without Deebo Samue l for their game against the Falcons. As you can see below, there are now five wide receivers unavailable for the 49ers. Demarcus Robinson - WR (ankle) Robinson suffered a high-ankle sprain in the team's Week 2 win over the Dolphins. He will miss significant time. Impact : Reports suggest Jacob Cowing will be leaned on to fill the void left behind by the injuries to Robinson and De'Zhaun Stribling . Expect Mike Evans , assuming health, Christian McCaffrey , and George Kittle to soak up additional volume. Deebo Samuel - WR (hamstring) Samuel suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 5 win over the Seahawks. He is expected to miss multiple weeks and was ruled out for Week 7 Friday. He reportedly has a chance to return in Week 9 following the team's Week 8 bye. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Brandin Cooks is the "next man up" for a 49ers team absolutely devastated by injuries. Cooks can be added from waivers after serving as the de facto WR2 opposite Mike Evans once Samuel departed. De’Zhaun Stribling - WR (ankle) Stribling suffered an ankle injury in the team's Week 1 win over the Rams. The 49ers placed him on injured reserve in Week 2 after he underwent surgery to repair a deltoid ligament tear. He is expected to return in 10 weeks. Impact: The Athletic's Matt Barrows believes Demarcus Robinson will be the primary beneficiary. Ricky Pearsall - WR (knee) Pearsall was placed on season-ending injured reserve. Impact: Pearsall will miss the entirety of the 2026 season. ◆ Seattle Seahawks Rashid Shaheed - WR (knee) Shaheed injured his knee during a collision with teammate Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Week 7. Head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that the "early returns are positive" on his injury. He was ruled out for Week 8 Saturday. Impact: An absence theoretically leaves additional opportunities for veteran Cooper Kupp.

stories.title: Cowboys rookie report: Caleb Downs, Malachi Lawrence hurt
stories.summary: What are your thoughts on the Cowboys rookies right now?
stories.detailText: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas had another win within reach, but a fourth-quarter embarrassment ended in a 33–30 overtime loss to Arizona. For the rookie class, LT Overton supplied a takeaway, Malachi Lawrence generated some pressure, and Caleb Downs’ afternoon ended early with a concussion. But here is how each rookie fared this week, listed in draft order, and any undrafted players worth noting after that. Caleb Downs (55 defensive snaps | 4 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 QB hits | 0 pressures) Downs offered some resistance against the run and was credited with two run stops, one extremely impressive one on fourth down on the goal line. His coverage was less encouraging with all three targets against him completed for 49 yards. His day then ended after he suffered a concussion attempting to tackle Tyler Allgeier on the running back’s fourth-quarter touchdown reception. There were useful contributions near the line, but too much production allowed through the air. Malachi Lawrence (40 defensive snaps | 0 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 1 QB hit | 2 pressures) Lawrence’s pass rush provided more than his empty tackle column suggests. He produced two pressures on 24 pass-rush snaps and registered a quarterback hit, although he could not turn those opportunities into a sack. Across 40 defensive snaps, Dallas needed more finishing production from its first-round edge defender, especially when it mattered most in the closing portion of the game. He injured his ankle in the game and could miss some time. Jaishawn Barham (16 defensive snaps | 1 tackle | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 QB hits ) Barham had a limited role behind Shemar James and DeMarvion Overshown. His coverage results were modestly encouraging allowing one reception for six yards on two targets. However, one tackle and no plays behind the line made this another quiet outing. His small workload limits how much can be concluded about the performance. LT Overton (39 total snaps | 0 tackles | 0 TFL | 0 sacks | 0 INT | 0 passes defended | 0 QB hits | 1 pressure | 1 fumble recovery) Overton delivered the rookie group’s clearest positive when he recovered Bam Knight’s fumble after Overshown forced the ball loose late in the second quarter. Securing that possession mattered. His work elsewhere was quieter, with one pressure on 19 pass-rush snaps and no tackles or sacks. The recovery was valuable, but Dallas still needs more consistent disruption from his defensive opportunities. Camden Brown (10 ST snaps | 0 targets | 0 receptions | 0 receiving yards | 0 TD) Brown’s involvement remained almost entirely on special teams. With just one offensive snap and no targets, there was no meaningful receiving performance to evaluate. Staying involved on game day is a step forward, but his offensive opportunity remains extremely limited.

teamStories.summary: Last week’s “quarterback controversy” shifts to the running backs
teamStories.detailText: (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders managed to start November right by getting a win and ending a four-game losing streak, taking down the New York Jets 38-33 . Meanwhile, a running back change where Mike Washington Jr. became the lead back and Ashton Jeanty was the third-down option in New York leads the discussion surrounding the Raiders in the Week 9 NFL Power Rankings. Sports Illustrated 17. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 22 I can’t be the only one who saw Klint Kubiak open the door just a smidge for Mike Washington Jr. and watched as Washington kicked the thing open, right? It’s a different feel when the rookie out of Arkansas is in the backfield. — Conor Orr Since I mentioned the stacked boxes (eight or more defenders) that each running back has faced in defense of Jeanty in the past, it’s only right that I circle back to it now that Washington has had a chance to be the RB1. Per Next Gen Stats , Jeanty still has faced the fifth-highest rate of stacked boxes among qualifying running backs at 29.6%. However, that figure has come down since the beginning of the season, sitting at or below 30% every game since Week 4. To be fair, Las Vegas playing from behind in the majority of those contests is a big factor. That being said, the Silver and Black were trailing in a good portion of the Jets game, and Washington faced a stacked box on 48.0% of his carries , tied for the fourth-highest rate in Week 8. According to Sumer Sports , Washington is averaging 2.9 ypc (27 carries for 78 yards) on such carries, while Jeanty is at 2.6 ypc (43 carries, 113 yards) . The biggest difference between the two is that the rookie has a slight advantage in rushing yards over expected (RYOE) per attempt: +0.4 to -0.3, according to NGS . That’s something to monitor as the former’s workload (presumptively) continues to increase over the coming weeks. NFL.com 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 25 The aerial stylings of Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers and the rest of the crew delivered again, ending the Raiders’ four-game losing skid in a wild, back-and-forth affair in MetLife Stadium. Like much of Las Vegas’ 2026 season, I certainly didn’t expect one development to emerge: rookie Mike Washington Jr. has taken over as the bell cow in Silver and Black, while Ashton Jeanty has become Klint Kubiak’s preferred third-down, pass-catching back — and is making a difference. He played a big part in the Raiders’ comeback win Sunday and at least adds a bit of dynamism to the unit. — Nick Shook The irony of Jeanty getting demoted to the third-down role is that he’s been one of the best receiving backs in the league. He leads the position with 37 catches, 376 yards (82 more than anyone else) and three receiving TDs (tied with Bhayshul Tuten). That’s on top of ranking fifth (minimum 50 total touches) in yards per reception (10.16) and ninth in EPA per target (0.16), according to Sumer . For the record, of the eight running backs that have a higher EPA/target than Jeanty, only Chuba Hubbard has at least 20 targets (26), while Jeanty is sitting at 48 to bring down his average. But, of course, the Raiders didn’t make the Boise State product the No. 6 pick in the draft to play a complementary role… The Athletic 19. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 24 Reality check: Ashton Jeanty may not bounce back It was a tough week for Jeanty. After he made disparaging comments about the Jets, ESPN commentator and former Jets head coach Rex Ryan called him “soft as Charmin.” On Sunday, the No. 6 pick in the 2025 draft was essentially benched for rookie Mike Washington. Jeanty finished with two carries for 9 yards, while Washington had 25 for 83. — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff I have a hard time buying that Jeanty’s comments were the only reason why Kubiak reduced his role in what was a pivotal game for the team’s playoff hopes. But I also won’t deny that the remarks played a factor in the decision. If the 25-2 carry split/ratio continues against the San Francisco 49ers this weekend, that’s a strong sign Jeanty wasn’t just being punished or disciplined this past Sunday. Bleacher Report 17. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 The Las Vegas Raiders were well-prepared for their second trip to the East Coast this season. They fell behind early, but Kirk Cousins showed why he still gives the Silver and Black the best chance to win, throwing for 247 yards and three touchdowns and scoring a touchdown on a quarterback sneak. For now, head coach Klint Kubiak is trying to stay in the playoff picture, so expect Cousins to keep the starting job for the foreseeable future. Rookie first-rounder Fernando Mendoza’s time will come, but the .500 Raiders should keep riding Cousins’ arm for now. The Raiders are a flawed team with an inefficient ground attack, averaging three yards per carry, and a leaky defense, but Cousins and the passing game give them a chance to pull off victories. — Moe Moton B/R starts to reverse course here, primarily focusing on last week’s theme with the “quarterback controversy” between Cousins and Mendoza . I mentioned this last week; beating the Jets likely keeps Cousins behind center for two more games since the Raiders will still be “in the hunt”. Additionally, there’s more momentum that Mendoza’s first start comes after the Week 13 bye. ESPN 20. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 22 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: DB Mike Haynes in 1983 The Raiders bolstered their secondary by acquiring Haynes from the Patriots. The move was instrumental to winning a title that season, as he recorded an interception, two pass breakups and a tackle in Super Bowl XVIII against Washington. Haynes, who was elected to the Hall of Fame in 1997, went on to play seven seasons with the Silver and Black. In 87 games (72 starts), he totaled 18 interceptions. — Ryan McFadden ESPN took a very different approach to their Power Ranking analysis, choosing to play on the upcoming trade deadline and focus on nostalgia. McFadden hit the nail right on the head because Haynes is considered one of the best in-season trade acquisitions in NFL history, not just the Raiders’ history. Also, I can’t think of a better one off the top of my head because the organization has primarily been a seller, if anything, at the deadline during my lifetime. For what it’s worth, when I asked Google AI for the best Raiders in-season trade acquisition, Haynes came up first and Carson Palmer was second. Palmer is on the wrong end of two of the worst trades in franchise history, or at least the last 15 to 20 years. The Raiders gave up first- and second-round picks to get the quarterback out of retirement and away from the Cincinnati Bengals in a desperation move after starter Jason Campbell suffered an injury while the team was 4-2 in 2011. Palmer had a 4-5 record down the stretch, and the club missed the playoffs that year. The Silver and Black went 4-12 the following season and traded Palmer, along with a seventh-round pick, to the Arizona Cardinals for sixth- and seventh-round selections. He had a 38-21-1 record in Arizona , earning a second-team All-Pro bid and leading the Cardinals to the playoffs in 2015.

headlines.summary: Norchad Omier and the Minnesota Timberwolves have agreed upon a Two-Way contract. In a related move, the Wolves have waived Enrique Freeman from his Two-Way. Freeman is currently out for a few weeks due to injury. Omier averaged 18.3 points, 11.4 rebounds and 2.5 assists in the G League last season. Freeman averaged 16.5 points, 8.7 rebounds and 2.4 assists last season with the Iowa Wolves.

headlines.title: Lendeborg's start has the Warriors rethinking
headlines.summary: Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg scored 37 points with six threes in the Warriors' 124–112 win over the Clippers. Steve Kerr took him out with two minutes to play, after the Clippers cut a 21-point lead to eight. Lendeborg had been chasing 40 points. Golden State is 4–3, and CBS Sports calls his start one of the most impressive in NBA history.

headlines.title: Grizzlies are the only unbeaten team
headlines.summary: Memphis is 6–0 after six straight wins and is the only team in the league still unbeaten. The Grizzlies lead the NBA in net rating at +15.1 after two weeks, ahead of Houston, Portland, Minnesota and Boston. Yahoo Sports notes they tore down their core over the summer.

headlines.title: Thunder to retire Westbrook's No. 0
headlines.summary: The Thunder will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0 on February 7, when they host the Knicks. Westbrook played the first 11 of his 18 seasons in Oklahoma City, won MVP and averaged a triple-double in three straight seasons. The game and ceremony will air on NBC and stream on Peacock.

headlines.title: Grizzlies roll over the winless Kings
headlines.summary: Memphis beat Sacramento 136–105. Cameron Boozer scored 27 points with nine rebounds, and the Grizzlies are off to a 6-0 start. Darius Acuff Jr. led Sacramento with 38 points, nine three-pointers, five rebounds and five assists, but it wasn't enough. Acuff is averaging 26.3 points per game, the most among NBA rookies. The Kings have lost six straight and are still winless.

headlines.title: Maxey's 38 points carry 76ers past Hornets
headlines.summary: Philadelphia beat Charlotte 109–104. Tyrese Maxey scored 38 points with four rebounds and four assists. Grayson Allen had 27 points and seven threes for the Hornets, and Brandon Miller added 24 points, five rebounds and five assists. The Hornets lost a close game despite a strong effort from both players.

headlines.title: Rockets bounce back against Thunder
headlines.summary: Houston beat Oklahoma City 119–98. Jabari Smith Jr. scored 30 points with nine rebounds, five assists and six three-pointers, and Marcus Smart added 24 points and seven threes. Alperen Sengun had 16 points and nine assists.

headlines.title: Holmgren's injury leaves the Thunder short-handed
headlines.summary: Chet Holmgren is out 8 to 10 weeks with a knee injury, according to ESPN. Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace are also set to miss extended time, so Oklahoma City has lost three key players early in the season. The Thunder are no longer signing free agent Ochai Agbaji and are reconsidering their open roster spot. Rookie Aday Mara becomes a bigger part of the rotation, and CBS Sports reports there are trade rumours swirling around the team.

headlines.title: Jeanie Buss accuses her siblings of conspiring against her
headlines.summary: In a court filing this week, Jeanie Buss accused Joey and Jesse Buss of a 'cloak and dagger' campaign through the media. She said they were jealous that their father chose her to govern the Lakers. The siblings want to sell their remaining shares to an ownership group led by Bob Iger and Josh Kushner, which is buying the team from Mark Walter at a $12.5 billion valuation. Buss has asked a judge to block the sale. A hearing is set for 8 December in Los Angeles Superior Court.

headlines.title: Lamar Jackson out after thumb surgery
headlines.summary: Lamar Jackson is out with a right thumb injury that requires surgery. Backup Tyler Huntley also went down in Sunday's loss to the Bills. Baltimore has added QB Austin Reed to the practice squad. The Ravens have lost three straight games and are 4–4.

headlines.title: Jack Campbell still in hospital
headlines.summary: Lions linebacker Jack Campbell remains in hospital for evaluation and monitoring of a neck injury suffered against the Vikings. The team says 'preliminary indications are positive'. Lions coach Dan Campbell called Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell a 'class act' for his actions after the injury.

headlines.title: Aiyuk hires Rosenhaus, wants back in NFL
headlines.summary: Brandon Aiyuk has hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, who says he is working on getting Aiyuk back to work and playing in the NFL. Aiyuk has not played since October 20, 2024, when he tore his right ACL, MCL and meniscus. The 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list in December after he stopped attending the facility.

headlines.title: Colts stick with Daniel Jones
headlines.summary: Coach Shane Steichen says Daniel Jones will start Week 9 against the Cowboys, despite a 42–7 loss to the Jaguars. Jones threw two more interceptions, taking his season total to nine. His 39.6 QBR is the second-worst of his eight seasons. Steichen says the offence's problems go beyond Jones.

headlines.title: Lions end the Vikings' unbeaten run
headlines.summary: Detroit beat Minnesota 19–15 at home, handing the NFL's last undefeated team its first loss. Gibbs scored on a 30-yard, tackle-breaking run in the third quarter. Goff found Williams for a 7-yard touchdown late in the fourth. Goff finished 18 of 25 for 176 yards with his first interception of the season. Kyler Murray went 17 of 29 for 210 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The Vikings were outgained 384 yards to 266 and had only 81 rushing yards. Minnesota's defence had four sacks of Goff but couldn't hold a late lead.

headlines.title: Lamar Jackson hurt on the first play as Ravens fall to Bills
headlines.summary: Jackson hurt his right thumb on his first snap of his first game back from a high ankle sprain, which kept him out for three games. He was ruled out for the rest of the 36–10 loss to Buffalo. Backup Tyler Huntley also left with a toe injury. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano went 10 of 21 for 91 yards with an interception. Derrick Henry ran 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown. ESPN's injury piece says this is the most injury-filled season of Jackson's nine-year career.

headlines.title: Buccaneers win 16–0 without completing a pass
headlines.summary: Baker Mayfield was 0 of 3 in the rain, but Tampa Bay beat Atlanta 16–0 on the ground. Bucky Irving ran for 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries. Kenny Gainwell added 140 yards on 25 carries. The Buccaneers rushed for 324 yards, a team record for a single game. They became the first team since Buffalo in September 1974 to finish a game with zero completions. Michael Penix Jr. was 8 of 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions for Atlanta.
